item.title: Colombia aprueba un aumento presupuestario del 16% tras la advertencia fiscal del FMI
item.description: Tanto el Senado como la Cámara de Diputados han dado luz verde a un presupuesto para 2027 de COP$635 billones (US$201.000 millones) propuesto por el Gobierno.
item.dc:creator: Oscar Medina
item.content:encoded: Bogotá — los legisladores colombianos aprobaron este martes por la mañana un aumento presupuestario del 16%, lo que ha agravado la preocupación de los inversores por la creciente carga de la deuda del país. Tanto el Senado como la Cámara de Diputados han dado luz verde a un presupuesto para 2027 de COP$635 billones (US$201.000 millones) propuesto por el Gobierno. Los rendimientos de los bonos colombianos se han disparado desde que el Gobierno dio a conocer su plan de gasto en agosto. Nigel Chalk, director del Departamento del Hemisferio Occidental del Fondo Monetario Internacional, afirmó la semana pasada que la situación fiscal del país es «insostenible». El presidente colombiano, Abelardo De la Espriella, asumió el cargo en agosto y se encuentra actualmente en negociaciones para un nuevo programa del FMI que le ayude a hacer frente al desastre fiscal que le dejó su predecesor. Su administración afirma que el aumento presupuestario es necesario para cubrir unos gastos superiores a lo previsto en materia de sanidad, pensiones y pagos de intereses, entre otras obligaciones. Los legisladores mantuvieron el gasto total sin cambios respecto a la propuesta del Gobierno, pero reasignaron COP$8,4 billones del servicio de la deuda a la inversión y a la respuesta al devastador terremoto que azotó el oeste de Colombia en agosto. Colombia recibirá en noviembre en Bogotá a una misión técnica del FMI para continuar las conversaciones exploratorias sobre el apoyo a sus esfuerzos de estabilización fiscal, en su intento por abordar lo que el ministro de Hacienda, Miguel Gómez, describió como una situación fiscal crítica. “Este es el primer paso para comenzar a recuperar la estabilidad de nuestra economía”, declaró Gómez tras la aprobación del proyecto de ley en la Cámara Baja a primera hora del martes. “Para generar el crecimiento y la prosperidad que esperamos que se produzcan en los próximos años”. La atención se centrará ahora en si el Gobierno de De la Espriella logrará obtener la aprobación del Congreso para un plan de ajuste equivalente a más del 2 % del producto interior bruto. Sin medidas correctivas, el déficit podría superar el 9 % del PIB el próximo año, según las propias previsiones del Gobierno. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

item.title: Diesel russo retorna à Turquia e ao Brasil após fim de veto às exportações
item.description: Os carregamentos de diesel russo estão retornando aos seus destinos tradicionais depois que os Estados Unidos suspenderam as sanções e garantiram o fim da proibição de exportação, com pelo menos dois navios-tanque indicando viagens para a Turquia e o Brasil nos últimos dias, de acordo com dados de transporte marítimo da Kpler e da LSEG.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os carregamentos de diesel russo estão retornando aos seus destinos tradicionais depois que os Estados Unidos suspenderam as sanções e garantiram o fim da proibição de exportação, com pelo menos dois navios-tanque indicando viagens para a Turquia e o Brasil nos últimos dias, de acordo com dados de transporte marítimo da Kpler e da LSEG. A Rússia suspendeu, em 9 de outubro, a proibição autoimposta às exportações de diesel — introduzida para lidar com a escassez interna provocada por ataques de drones ucranianos a refinarias —, após fechar um acordo com o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, para fornecer diesel aos mercados globais. O acordo incluiu o levantamento temporário das sanções dos EUA ao fornecimento de combustível russo, embora os embargos da UE e do Reino Unido às importações de combustível russo continuem em vigor. Trump está empenhado em tentar acalmar os preços do diesel antes das eleições de meio de mandato, em 3 de novembro. O diesel é um combustível essencial utilizado na indústria, na agricultura e no transporte. Normalmente o segundo maior exportador mundial de diesel, atrás apenas dos Estados Unidos, a Rússia já havia reduzido suas exportações no verão, antes de impor a proibição de exportação. EXPORTAÇÕES RUSSAS DE DIESEL CAÍRAM 41% ESTE ANO As exportações totais de diesel da Rússia ficaram em torno de 345.000 bpd neste ano até o momento, uma queda de 41% em relação ao ano passado, segundo os dados. O petroleiro Leruo indicava Manaus, no Brasil, como seu destino após partir do porto russo de Primorsk, no Mar Báltico, em 16 de outubro, segundo os dados. O petroleiro Dolunay, que partiu de Primorsk com uma carga de diesel em 14 de outubro, está a caminho de Alanya, na Turquia. Cada um dos dois petroleiros transporta cargas de 300.000 barris de diesel, segundo a Kpler. Marrocos também começou a importar diesel russo desde o fim da proibição de exportação. A Turquia recebeu cerca de 34% dos carregamentos de diesel russo neste ano até o momento, o Brasil 24% e Marrocos 10%, segundo dados da Kpler. “Com o retorno do abastecimento russo, as rotas comerciais estabelecidas são o destino mais lógico para esses barris inicialmente. Também espero que a Rússia priorize clientes que possam absorver volumes significativos rapidamente, em vez de perder tempo desenvolvendo novos mercados quando a disponibilidade global de diesel continua escassa”, disse a chefe de risco geopolítico da Kpler, Michelle Brouhard. Fornecedores turcos de combustível reduziram as compras de diesel de refinarias nacionais em antecipação ao recebimento das exportações russas, disseram à Reuters três fontes familiarizadas com o assunto. A Tupras e a Socar, que operam as principais refinarias da Turquia, não responderam a um pedido de comentário. RÚSSIA AFIRMA QUE PODE AUMENTAR DRASTICAMENTE AS EXPORTAÇÕES DE DIESEL Trump afirmou que a Rússia exportaria imediatamente 300 mil toneladas, ou 2,25 milhões de barris, seguidas por 500 mil toneladas em novembro e 1 milhão de toneladas “imediatamente depois”. O vice-primeiro-ministro Alexander Novak disse na semana passada que as exportações russas poderiam ultrapassar os níveis acordados com Trump, com meta de até 3,5 milhões de toneladas por mês (875.000 bpd) até o final do ano. Os volumes que Trump disse que a Rússia forneceria são modestos em comparação com o déficit global, mas, nos níveis discutidos por Novak, eles cobririam a maior parte da lacuna, afirmou o analista da Sparta Commodities, James Noel-Beswick. Os preços dos futuros de diesel de referência europeus não sofreram alterações significativas desde o acordo, de acordo com dados da LSEG, e eram negociados com um prêmio de US$80 em relação ao petróleo Brent nesta terça-feira. Esse valor ficou abaixo das máximas históricas de quase US$95 registradas no final de setembro, mas ainda é várias vezes superior ao de um ano atrás. Os embarques de diesel russo totalizaram cerca de 210 mil toneladas, ou 1,56 milhão de barris, entre 11 e 20 de outubro, segundo a Kpler.

item.title: Shark kills woman swimming off South Africa's Eastern Cape
item.description: A 65-year-old woman was killed by a shark at a popular beach off the coast of South Africa's Eastern Cape province on Tuesday, local authorities said.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A 65-year-old woman was killed by a shark at a popular beach off the coast of South Africa's Eastern Cape province on Tuesday, local authorities said. "A fatal shark attack occurred at the Orient Beach this morning, resulting in a tragic loss of a swimmer," a spokesperson for the local municipality told Reuters. The woman was swimming with a group when she indicated she was in trouble, a witness told public broadcaster SABC. "We all realised she'd been bitten by a shark, and she was in a very bad way," the witness said. "The bites were very severe, but there were only two, one on her thigh and one on her upper arm." He said the woman was brought back to shore, where she was declared dead on the beach. Eastern Cape police said officers who attended the scene found her body with open wounds and opened an inquest. The species of shark involved was not immediately known. Buffalo City municipality has closed Orient Beach and nearby Eastern Beach until further notice and urged people to exercise caution. South Africa's coast has many shark species, but it is popularly known for great white sharks, which draw tourists worldwide for cage diving and shark-watching trips.

Moller-Maersk, and Vietnam's Hateco Group signed a non-binding agreement to study the development and operation of railway freight terminals in northern Vietnam, the Vietnamese government said on Tuesday. • The agreement was signed in the presence of Vietnam's General Secretary and President To Lam during his visit to Denmark • The companies will study a railway freight terminal in Hai Phong, including cargo-handling and storage facilities, as well as three additional rail freight locations in northern Vietnam, according to a statement on the Vietnamese government portal

item.title: Russian diesel returns to Turkey, Brazil after export ban lifted, shipping data shows
item.description: Russian diesel cargoes are returning to their traditional destinations after the US suspended sanctions and secured the lifting of an export ban, with at least two tankers signalling trips to Turkey and Brazil in recent days, according to shipping data from Kpler and LSEG.
item.dc:creator: Robert Harvey, Enes Tunagur, Ahmad Ghaddar
item.content:encoded: Russian diesel cargoes are returning to their traditional destinations after the US suspended sanctions and secured the lifting of an export ban, with at least two tankers signalling trips to Turkey and Brazil in recent days, according to shipping data from Kpler and LSEG. Russia lifted its self-imposed ban on October 9 on diesel exports, introduced to tackle domestic shortages triggered by Ukrainian drone attacks on refineries, after [USN:L1N45V0MW TEXT:"striking a deal"] with US President Donald Trump to supply diesel to global markets. The deal included a temporary lifting of US sanctions on Russian fuel supply, though EU and UK embargoes on Russian fuel imports remain in force. Trump has set his sights on trying to calm diesel prices ahead of the [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterm elections"] on November 3. Diesel is a key fuel used in industry, agriculture and transportation. Usually the world's second-largest exporter of diesel after the United States, Russia had already reduced its exports in summer before imposing the export ban. RUSSIAN DIESEL EXPORTS DOWN 41% THIS YEAR Total Russian diesel exports were around 345,000 bpd over this year so far, down 41% from last year, the data show. The tanker Leruo was signalling Manaus, Brazil, as its destination after departing from Russia's Baltic port of Primorsk on October 16, the data showed. The tanker Dolunay, which departed Primorsk with a diesel cargo on October 14, is heading for Alanya, Turkey. The two tankers are each carrying 300,000-barrel diesel cargoes, according to Kpler. [USN:L6N4600IE TEXT:"Morocco"] has also begun importing Russian diesel since the lifting of the export ban. Turkey has received around 34% of Russian diesel loadings so far this year, Brazil 24% and Morocco 10%, according to Kpler data. ”With Russian supply returning, established trade routes are the most logical place for those barrels to go first. I would also expect Russia to prioritise customers that can absorb meaningful volumes quickly, rather than spend time developing new outlets when global diesel availability remains tight,” said Kpler’s head of geopolitical risk, Michelle Brouhard. Turkish fuel suppliers have reduced purchases of diesel from domestic refineries in anticipation of receiving Russian exports, three sources familiar with the matter told Reuters. Tupras and Socar, which operate Turkey’s major refineries, did not respond to a request for comment. RUSSIA SAYS IT COULD RAISE DIESEL EXPORTS SHARPLY Trump said Russia would immediately export 300,000 metric tons, or 2.25 million barrels, followed by 500,000 tons in November and 1 million tons "immediately thereafter". Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak said last week that [USN:L1N45Y0MF TEXT:"Russian exports could surpass "]the levels agreed with Trump, aiming for up to 3.5 million tons per month (875,000 bpd) by the end of the year. The volumes Trump said Russia would supply are modest in comparison to the global shortfall, but at the levels Novak discussed, they would close most of the gap, Sparta Commodities analyst James Noel-Beswick said. Prices of European benchmark diesel futures have not changed significantly since the deal, according to LSEG data, and were trading at an $80 premium to Brent crude on Tuesday. This was off all-time highs of almost $95 in late September, but still several times higher than a year ago. Russian diesel loadings totalled around 210,000 tons, or 1.56 million barrels, over October 11-20, according to Kpler.

item.title: US Stocks: GE Aerospace raises 2026 profit forecast as services strength drives growth
item.description: GE Aerospace has increased its 2026 adjusted earnings forecast due to continued demand for engine maintenance. The demand for spare parts remains high, which supports their financial outlook. Airlines are facing rising fuel costs due to disruptions in oil supply and are adjusting their capacity accordingly. Despite potential pressures on flight schedules, GE Aerospace's revenue from services is expected to remain strong.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: GE Aerospace on Tuesday raised its 2026 profit forecast for the second time this year, betting strong demand for engine maintenance and spare parts will offset the impact of higher fuel costs on flights.Airlines worldwide are cutting costs and capacity to defend ticket prices after the war in Iran disrupted oil shipping routes, driving up jet fuel costs and adding to pressure on the industry.With no end to the war in sight, higher fuel prices are testing airlines' ability to maintain schedules and margins, raising the risk of fewer flights and weaker demand for maintenance.GE Aerospace has said, however, that any impact on services revenue and profit this year should be limited, as much of its 2026 engine shop-visit work is already under contract and demand for spare parts continues to outstrip supply.Last month, GE Aerospace finance chief Rahul Ghai said the company had seen no changes to airlines' fleet plans, while the number of parked aircraft remained low.The jet-engine maker now expects 2026 adjusted earnings of $8.00 to $8.10 per share, up from its prior forecast of $7.65 to $7.85, and above analysts' consensus estimate of $7.92, according to data compiled by LSEG. We are raising our 2026 guidance across the board, and we now expect 2027 commercial services to grow low-double-digits supported by our over $170 billion commercial services backlog, CEO Larry Culp said in a statement.Through CFM International, its joint venture with France's Safran, GE Aerospace is a leading supplier of engines for narrowbody jets and a major player in the widebody market. Parts and services account for more than 70% of its commercial engine revenue.Quarterly revenue at its commercial engines and services unit climbed 21% to $10.34 billion, driven by strong demand for aftermarket services. The company also raised its 2026 revenue growth forecast for the segment to the low 20% range, compared with its previous expectation of about 20% growth.It reported an adjusted profit of $2.25 per share for the quarter through September, beating Wall Street expectations of $2.01.Shares of the company rose nearly 1.2% in premarket trading.

item.title: US Stocks: GM's core profit rises 22% on strength of pickup-truck business
item.description: General Motors exceeded analyst expectations in third-quarter earnings, driven by robust demand for their pickups and SUVs. The company reported an adjusted EBIT of $4.1 billion, marking a 22% year-over-year increase. Despite facing inflationary challenges, GM forecasts an adjusted EBIT of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion by 2026. Additionally, a $20 billion stock buyback program was initiated to bolster share value.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: General Motors' third-quarter results easily beat analyst expectations on the back of resolute shoppers who continue to spring for pricey pickups and SUVs.The company on Tuesday said quarterly earnings before interest and tax, not including one-time items (adjusted EBIT) rose 22% from a year earlier, to $4.1 billion. That amounted to $3.70 per share, topping analyst expectations of $3.63, according to LSEG data.The automaker said it expected to end 2026 with adjusted EBIT in the range of $14.5 billion to $15.5 billion, narrowed from previous guidance of $14 billion to $16 billion. The company said it remained confident despite inflationary pressures from higher logistics and energy costs, tariffs and other expenses.GM shares fell about 6% in premarket trading.The company said its board approved a multi-year, $20 billion stock buyback program. GM has bought back about $29.5 billion of its own shares since 2023, driving down its overall share count to help its per-share profit results.GM in the third quarter sold a higher mix of large pickup trucks and fewer electric vehicles, which helped the bottom line. The automaker has been pulling back on sales of EVs, which historically have lost money, following the Trump administration's withdrawal of support for them.Revenue totaled $50 billion, up 2.9% from a year earlier. In North America, the company's profit margin improved to 8.7%, from 6.2% a year earlier, despite a slight decline in quarterly sales.GM said the path forward is more challenging, but reiterated that it expects next year's results to be better, assuming continued strong consumer demand and a moderating of cost pressures on commodities and logistics.

France’s fiscal crisis is nearing its breaking point

With debt approaching 120% of GDP and borrowing costs rising, France faces mounting pressure to rein in its deficit, but pension reform and spending cuts remain politically fraught ahead of the 2027 election, The Editorial Board writes for Bloomberg.

Bloomberg Editors

20 October, 2026 04:43 pm IST

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

F rance’s crisis keeps getting more extreme, spilling over the weekend into broader protests that precipitated hundreds of millions of euros in damage and nearly 2,400 arrests. The country’s leaders are rightly focused on curtailing the violence. Yet as they seek ways to placate a frustrated populace, they must be careful not to make a bad fiscal situation worse.

It’s hard to overstate how dire France’s finances have become, particularly now that worried investors have pushed its 10-year bond yields to almost 5%. If borrowing costs remain this high, the interest rate the government pays will soon exceed the economy’s nominal growth rate. As a result, just stabilizing sovereign debt — currently about 120% of gross domestic product, among the highest in Europe — could require running a sustained primary budget surplus of as much as 2% of GDP. That’s a feat France hasn’t achieved since the 1970s.

The politics of achieving the necessary deficit reduction, estimated to be at least €125 billion by 2032, could hardly be more fraught. Among potential savings and revenue measures, pension reform stands out: Increasing the retirement age to 65 — still below the norm among western European peers — could reap about €18 billion. Yet when President Emmanuel Macron in 2023 pushed through an (ultimately postponed) increase from 62 to 64, the move triggered some of the country’s largest-ever protests — albeit rivaled in violence by the weekend’s events — and contributed to the far-right National Rally party’s success in 2024 elections.

Show Full Article

With presidential elections coming next year, there’s even less appetite for prudence. The current minority government’s 2027 budget proposal, which would reduce the deficit by about €28 billion, faces stiff opposition. National Rally’s Marine Le Pen, who leads national polling for the next presidential election, sought to calm bond markets with a pledge of fiscal consolidation that contrasts sharply with the tax cuts and spending promises in her platform. Meanwhile, left-wing candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon, whose statements have been blamed for inflaming protesters, proposed simply canceling more than €500 billion in French public debt held by its central bank — an absurdity that, even if possible, would serve only to spook markets more.

Eventually, the nation’s leaders will have to recognize that there’s no alternative to boring, unpleasant budget discipline. The longer that takes, the greater the damage will be.

France’s malaise places it on a collision course with the broader European Union. The longer it delays serious reform, the more precarious its finances will become as it takes on more debt at higher yields. If investors ultimately refuse to lend, the EU and the European Central Bank will face a dilemma: Organize a bailout or let the bloc’s second-largest economy descend into financial chaos. The best-case scenario would entail imposing austerity measures on France potentially harsher than what’s now needed to stabilize its debt. The worst would be an acute crisis involving a French default, bank runs and possibly a breakup of the euro.

If France’s current minority government can’t act, hopefully the next election will produce leadership capable of delivering the difficult reform the country needs. Even populists have been known to act responsibly when confronted with the immutable facts of public finance. There’s no better way out.

Nine Years, Made Possible by Readers

In 2017, Shekhar Gupta started ThePrint with a simple belief: Indian readers want journalism that asks why and what next, not just what. And that enough of them would be willing to pay for good journalism.

Nine years on, that belief has held.

item.description:
Faith Hung Jeanny Kao
[台北 ２０日 ロイター] - 台湾経済部が２０日発表した９月の輸出受注額...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
台湾9月輸出受注、過去最高　2カ月連続1000億ドル超 10/20 20:07 配信

台湾・基隆港のコンテナ船、4月19日撮影 REUTERS/Edgar Su

Faith Hung　Jeanny Kao

[台北 ２０日 ロイター] - 台湾経済部が２０日発表した９月の輸出受注額は前年同月比６２．４％増の１１４２億１０００万ドルと、市場予想を上回る伸びとなった。台湾製の人工知能（ＡＩ）向け半導体やハイテク製品に対する世界的な需要に支えられた。

月間の受注額が１０００億ドルを超えるのは２カ月連続。８月は１０３０億ドルと、初めて１０００億ドルを突破した。

伸び率はアナリスト予想の５８．７％を上回り、前年比での増加は２０カ月連続となった。

経済部はＡＩ、高性能コンピューティング、クラウドサービス関連の旺盛な需要が寄与したと説明した。

１０月の輸出受注額は前年比６２．０─６７．０％増を見込む。通年では１兆１０００億ドルに達する可能性があるとした。

先行きについては、地政学リスクや通商政策などの不確実性が今後も世界経済の成長の重しになるとした。一方、台湾は半導体とサーバーのサプライチェーンで中核的な地位を占めており、受注は安定して伸び続けるとの見方を示した。

９月の品目別受注額は、通信機器の受注額が８７．３％増、電子製品は７１．０％増だった。

中国からの受注額は４８．５％増と、８月の４７．７％増から加速した。米国からの受注額は７９．４％増で、前月の８８．９％増から鈍化した。欧州からは６８．０％増、日本からは３５．５％増だった。

item.title: Protesting truck drivers put Italy's pasta production at risk
item.description: The production of Italian pasta is under threat as a protest by truck drivers in the south of the country over soaring fuel prices and the cost of living blocks deliveries to factories.
item.dc:creator: Sara Rossi, Francesca Piscioneri
item.content:encoded: The production of Italian pasta is under threat as a protest by truck drivers in the south of the country over soaring fuel prices and the cost of living blocks deliveries to factories. There are also growing concerns about food supplies in Rome, as transport bottlenecks hamper deliveries from southern Italy to the capital. Italian agriculture lobby group Confagricoltura warned that producers in Sicily would have to destroy large quantities of perishable products if transportation did not resume. Pasta maker Rummo, based in the Campania region, said on Tuesday it had suspended production after running out of ingredients. Almost all major pasta producers in the neighbouring region of Puglia, which together with Campania and Sicily form the heartland of Italy's pasta production, are facing similar difficulties, CEO Cosimo Rummo told daily la Repubblica. "This means that most of Italy's pasta production has ground to a halt, or is close to," he said. La Molisana, another producer based in the Molise region, said it had experienced a significant drop in production and had been forced to draw on its stocks of raw materials such as wheat and semola flour. Italy's pasta supply chain last year generated €13.5 billion in revenue, the European House-Ambrosetti (TEHA Group) said in a report in September. The Centro Agroalimentare Roma (CAR), Italy's largest wholesale fruit and vegetable market, said roadblocks and higher transport costs were causing shortages of products such as tomatoes, peppers and grapes, pushing up prices and increasing reliance on imports from countries including Spain and Albania. FOOD AND PETROL RUNNING OUT IN SOUTHERN ITALY The government is pledging more aid for road hauliers. After meeting with their representatives on Tuesday, Deputy Infrastructure Minister Edoardo Rixi said a package worth more than €150 million would be made available soon. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni's administration is also preparing [USN:L8N4660PD TEXT:"a security crackdown "]in response to weekend riots in Milan and other northern cities, which developed on the back of demonstrations against inflation. Vincenzo Aleccia, president of the Trapani trucking consortium in the western Sicilian port city, told Reuters that he knew the disruption was enormous but added that "it's a peaceful protest and it's for the benefit of the people," saying rising prices affected everyone. The protest, which began last week with the blocking of roads, motorways and ports in Sicily and the south, is causing shortages at supermarkets and queues at petrol stations. "People were trying to grab whatever was left. I had to go to a nearby town, and I also stocked up on flour and the food we consume most," said Zineb Boutimah, 45, who lives in Locri, a town in the southern province of Reggio Calabria. Elena Lombardo, 78, also from Locri, said her local petrol station attendant had urged her to fill up her tank on Monday, warning, "I don't know whether there will be any petrol tomorrow." On Tuesday, the petrol station was closed. ($1 = 0.8911 euros)

item.description:
Ankur Banerjee Stefanno Sulaiman
[シンガポール／ジャカルタ ２０日 ロイター] - ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
インドネシア株が反発、当局の対策発表でセンチメント改善 10/20 20:05 配信

インドネシア証券取引所の株価ボード、16日撮影 REUTERS/Ajeng Dinar Ulfiana

Ankur Banerjee　Stefanno Sulaiman

[シンガポール／ジャカルタ ２０日 ロイター] - ２０日のインドネシア株式市場は反発して引けた。指数算出会社ＭＳＣＩが同国をグローバル指数から除外する可能性を警告し、１６日と１９日の２営業日で１４．８％下落、時価総額８２０億ドルが失われる記録的な急落となったことを受け、当局が売りを制限する措置を導入した。

ジャカルタ総合指数は５．６％上昇して引けた。

海外投資家は２６年に入り、インドネシア株から既に５０億ドル近くを引き揚げた。ゴールドマン・サックスは、ＭＳＣＩによる指数からの除外で、パッシブ運用資金５６億ドルが流出する可能性があると推計している。

インドネシア証券取引所（ＩＤＸ）は１９日、ＭＳＣＩとオンライン会合を開いた後、特定の個人や法人などに株式保有が著しく集中している銘柄を、主要指数から除外すると発表した。

オールスプリング・グローバル・インベストメンツのポートフォリオマネジャー、ゲーリー・タン氏は、懸念の一部解消につながるが、国内で反発が起きる可能性を踏まえると実施が鍵になると指摘。「今後、資金フローに新たに生じるリスクは、パッシブファンドよりもアクティブファンドからの流出によるものが大きいと考えている」と語った。

ＭＳＣＩの警告はインドネシアルピアの重荷にもなっている。２０日は１米ドル＝１万７９８０ルピアに小幅上昇したものの、インドネシア中央銀行の金融政策決定を前に、６月に付けた過去最安値の１万８１９０ルピアに近い水準にとどまった。

中銀は２１日に金融政策を発表するが政策金利を据え置くと予想されている。ただ、一部のエコノミストは、年初来で７％下落しているルピアを防衛するため、利上げする可能性を指摘している。

格付け会社フィッチ・レーティングスのソブリン部門ディレクター、ジョージ・シュー氏は、今回の懸念と大幅な相場下落は、同社が３月にインドネシアの格付け見通しを「ネガティブ」に引き下げた際に指摘したリスクを改めて裏付けたと述べた。

「ソブリン格付けの観点からは、検討の発表自体が信用力に直ちに重大な影響を与えるとは予想していない」とする一方、対外的な圧力が政府の借り入れコストを押し上げ、対外的なショックへの備えを弱める可能性があると指摘した。

市場関係者は、株式保有が著しく集中する銘柄を主要指数から除外する措置について、建設的な一歩と評価。ただ、投資家は直接保有や投資信託などの金融商品を通じて、引き続きこれらの企業への投資リスクを抱えることになると指摘した。

証券会社キウム・セクリタス・インドネシアの調査責任者、リザ・カメリア・スルヤナタ氏は「銘柄がジャカルタ総合指数から除外されても、一般投資家が購入する商品の中で集中リスクが蓄積し続けることがないようにしなければならない」と述べた。

item.description: [２０日 ロイター] - 字節跳動（バイトダンス）、アリババ、騰訊（テンセント）の中国ＩＴ大手３社が、米半導体大手エヌビ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE-中国ＩＴ3社、エヌビディア新型カードを350億ドル超発注＝関係筋 10/20 19:59 配信

エヌビディアのロゴ、中国国際サプライチェーン博覧会で6月22日撮影 REUTERS/Florence Lo

[２０日 ロイター] - 字節跳動（バイトダンス）、アリババ、騰訊（テンセント）の中国ＩＴ大手３社が、米半導体大手エヌビディアの新型グラフィックスカード「ＲＴＸ ＰＲＯ ５５００」を計３００万枚超発注した。関係者２人が明らかにした。定価ベースの総額は３５０億ドルを超える。

ＲＴＸ ＰＲＯ ５５００はワークステーション向けの半導体だ。エヌビディアの最先端の人工知能（ＡＩ）半導体を使う大規模なデータセンターのコンピューター群に組み込むための製品ではない。最先端の製品より性能は劣るものの、米国の対中輸出規制に適合する同社製品の中では最も高性能な半導体の一つであるため、注文が殺到している。

関係者３人によると、中国企業はＲＴＸ ＰＲＯ ５５００を主にＡＩの推論に使おうとしている。推論とは、学習済みのモデルを動かし、チャットボットの応答などを生成する処理を指す。一般に、大量のデータを使ったモデルの学習ほど計算能力を必要としない。

関係者２人によると、中国ＩＴ大手３社が発注したカードの価格は１枚約１万１４００ドルで、注文総額は３５０億ドルを超える可能性がある。

＜供給ひっ迫＞

関係者３人によると、エヌビディアは中国のＩＴ企業からの需要が生産計画を大幅に上回っているため、注文に応じられる保証はないと顧客や取引先に伝えた。

関係者の１人によると、エヌビディアは取引先に対し、注文数量の５─１０％しか納入できない可能性があると伝えた。別の関係者によると、同社は２０２７年のＲＴＸ ＰＲＯ ５５００の生産枚数が世界全体で最大３００万枚にとどまるとの見通しを示した。関係者２人によると、中国の顧客からの注文は計６００万枚を超えている。

関係者２人によると、エヌビディアが全量の納入を約束できないのは、需要の急増に加え、優先的に生産する製品があるためだ。エヌビディアは２７年以降、台湾積体電路製造（ＴＳＭＣ）で確保する生産能力の多くを、大規模データセンター向けの次世代基盤「ルービン」に振り向ける見通しだという。

両関係者によると、エヌビディアは顧客に対し、ＲＴＸ ＰＲＯ ５５００の初期サンプルを１２月に提供し、２７年第１・四半期に商用出荷を始める予定だと伝えた。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：進む米中デカップリング、中国「保有米国債」の脅威減退か コラム：中国政府、株市場てこ入れ作戦に公的年金基金も動員 焦点：中国株、ＧＤＰ発表後も買い不発　不動産低迷で慎重ムード コラム：経済モデル転換目指す中国、不動産不況でも資源需要衰えず コラム：「カメ」の米国株が「ウサギ」の中国を追い抜く時 最終更新: 10/20(火) 19:59 ロイター

item.title: Qualcomm to cut jobs worldwide in performance-focused layoffs, internal memo shows
item.description: Qualcomm will cut jobs globally in a "performance-focused reduction" following its annual employee reviews, CEO Cristiano Amon told staff in a memo on Monday reviewed by Reuters, with notifications set to begin in November.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Soni, Jaspreet Singh
item.content:encoded: Qualcomm (QCOM.O) will cut jobs globally in a "performance-focused reduction" following its annual employee reviews, CEO Cristiano Amon told staff in a memo on Monday reviewed by Reuters, with notifications set to begin in November. The cuts are part of an effort to build "a stronger performance culture" and address situations where the company "has consistently fallen short of expectations," Amon said. The memo did not say how many jobs would be affected, and Reuters could not immediately determine the scale of the cuts. Qualcomm did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It had about 52,000 employees globally as of September last year, most of them full-time. Its financial year typically ends in late September. One of the world's biggest smartphone chipmakers, Qualcomm has been hit this year by a slump in consumer electronics sales as soaring memory prices weigh on demand in key markets. Its shares have risen just 1.5% in 2026, compared with gains of more than 12% for the benchmark S&P 500 (.SPX) and nearly 60% for the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (.SOX) . Qualcomm shares were up more than 1% after trading down about 0.5% earlier on Tuesday. In its latest earnings report in late July, Qualcomm forecast quarterly profit [USN:L6N43V1B5 TEXT:"below estimates"] and said revenue from Apple products would decline faster than expected, while signaling that growth in data-center and other non-handset businesses would more than offset the lost revenue by fiscal 2027. The company expects the majority of its chip sales to come from businesses other than smartphones in fiscal 2027 as it expands into the fast-growing AI data-center market. Amon said in the memo business priorities, organizational needs, skills and expertise would be considered in making the cuts. "As we have expanded the business, so have the competencies and skills we require," he wrote. "We must have the right people in the right roles so they can perform at their best and the company can continue to succeed."

Oct 20 : Qualcomm will cut jobs globally in a "performance-focused reduction" following its annual employee reviews, CEO Cristiano Amon told staff in a memo on Monday reviewed by Reuters, with notifications set to begin in November. The cuts are part of an effort to build "a stronger performance culture" and address situations where the company "has consistently fallen short of expectations," Amon said. The memo did not say how many jobs would be affected, and Reuters could not immediately determine the scale of the cuts. Qualcomm did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It had about 52,000 employees globally as of September last year, most of them full-time. Its financial year typically ends in late September.

One of the world's biggest smartphone chipmakers, Qualcomm has been hit this year by a slump in consumer electronics sales as soaring memory prices weigh on demand in key markets. Its shares have risen just 1.5 per cent in 2026, compared with gains of more than 12 per cent for the benchmark S&P 500 and nearly 60 per cent for the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index. Qualcomm shares were up more than 1 per cent after trading down about 0.5 per cent earlier on Tuesday. In its latest earnings report in late July, Qualcomm forecast quarterly profit below estimates and said revenue from Apple products would decline faster than expected, while signaling that growth in data-center and other non-handset businesses would more than offset the lost revenue by fiscal 2027. The company expects the majority of its chip sales to come from businesses other than smartphones in fiscal 2027 as it expands into the fast-growing AI data-center market. Amon said in the memo business priorities, organizational needs, skills and expertise would be considered in making the cuts. "As we have expanded the business, so have the competencies and skills we require," he wrote. "We must have the right people in the right roles so they can perform at their best and the company can continue to succeed."

item.title: Halliburton expects years-long oilfield demand from Gulf energy infrastructure rebuild
item.description: Halliburton forecast mid-single-digit revenue growth in 2027, expecting efforts to restore energy production and rebuild inventories in the war-hit Middle East to support demand for oilfield equipment, even as North America remains subdued.
item.dc:creator: Pranav Mathur
item.content:encoded: Halliburton (HAL.N) forecast mid-single-digit revenue growth in 2027, expecting efforts to restore energy production and rebuild inventories in the war-hit Middle East to support demand for oilfield equipment, even as North America remains subdued. Operating margins for the coming year will be about 15%, Chief Executive Jeff Miller said on Tuesday, an improvement of around 200 basis points. The forecast does not assume a recovery in US hydraulic fracturing activity. "This forecast includes a flat North America and no recovery in the domestic frac market, pointing to recovery in the Middle East and better margins post new contract start-ups abroad," said Citibank analyst Scott Gruber. Shares were up 2.4% after Halliburton beat third-quarter profit and revenue estimates. The US-Iran conflict, which is in its eighth month, has disrupted energy operations in the Middle East, delaying projects but potentially creating long-term demand for oilfield services. Consultancy Rystad Energy in April projected as much as $58 billion in repair costs for energy-linked infrastructure. "I expect the work to restore production, rebuild inventories and strengthen energy security will drive multi-year demand growth for oilfield services," Miller said. Quarterly revenue in the Middle East and Asia was broadly unchanged at $1.41 billion, Halliburton said. The company derives about a quarter of its total revenue from the Middle East. Revenue from the Middle East is expected to rise sequentially and year-over-year in the fourth quarter, Chief Operating Officer Shannon Slocum said on a post-earnings call. Outside the Middle East, international business is expected to grow about 12% this year, with Halliburton also anticipating solid growth in Venezuela, Slocum said. Oilfield service companies are rehiring workers and putting more equipment on the ground, as a US-backed multibillion-dollar plan to [USN:L6N46015P TEXT:"revive the country's battered"] oil industry gathers momentum. Latin America and Europe/Africa quarterly revenue rose 12.6% and 22.7%, respectively, in the third quarter, helping offset a 9% decline in North America due to weaker US pressure pumping activity. Total quarterly revenue rose 1.8% to $5.7 billion, topping analysts' estimates of $5.6 billion. Halliburton posted adjusted earnings of 60 cents per share for the three months ended September 30, beating analysts' average estimate of 58 cents, according to data compiled by LSEG. The company expects fourth-quarter profit between 62 cents and 64 cents, compared with analysts' estimates of 64 cents.

item.title: Prudential sheds Brazil, Mexico units to CNP for $4 billion as it narrows its focus
item.description: Prudential Financial said on Tuesday it would sell its Brazil and Mexico units to French insurance group CNP Assurances Group for $4.03 billion in cash as part of its ongoing push to simplify its business.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Prudential Financial (PRU.N) said on Tuesday it would sell its Brazil and Mexico units to French insurance group CNP Assurances Group for $4.03 billion in cash as part of its ongoing push to simplify its business. The deal adds momentum to Prudential's retreat from emerging markets — following divestitures in Indonesia, South Africa, and Kenya — as the US insurer sharpens focus on core businesses. In August, CEO Andy Sullivan said Prudential planned to slash the geographic footprint of its retirement and insurance businesses from more than a dozen countries to about half that number. Announcing the sale on Tuesday, Sullivan said, "We remain focused on narrowing our geographic footprint and building a simpler, more focused Prudential." The firm has operations in the United States, Asia, Europe and Latin America and roughly $1.6 trillion in assets as of June 30. Prudential will use the deal proceeds to invest in growth opportunities in retirement, asset management and select protection businesses in the US, Japan and select European markets. For CNP Assurances, the deal marks a major step in diversifying its Latin America business. The transaction is expected to close in the second half of 2027. Morgan Stanley served as financial adviser to Prudential, while Goldman Sachs advised CNP Assurances.

item.title: GM shares sink as automaker signals rising cost pressures
item.description: General Motors' third-quarter core profit rose sharply on the back of strong pickup truck sales, but its shares fell on Tuesday after the automaker signaled pressure in coming months from higher commodity costs and lower truck sales.
item.dc:creator: Kalea Hall, Nathan Gomes
item.content:encoded: General Motors' (GM.N) third-quarter core profit rose sharply on the back of strong pickup truck sales, but its shares fell on Tuesday after the automaker signaled pressure in coming months from higher commodity costs and lower truck sales. The company said quarterly earnings before interest and tax, not including one-time items (adjusted EBIT), rose 22% from a year earlier, to $4.1 billion. That amounted to $3.70 per share, topping analyst expectations of $3.63, according to LSEG data. It tightened its annual adjusted earnings-per-share forecast to between $12.75 and $13.75, the midpoint of which is below analysts' estimates of $13.41, according to data compiled by LSEG. GM shares fell about 5% in morning trading. "We think the selloff primarily reflects disappointment with the fact that the midpoint of its updated guidance is below" Wall Street's consensus, CFRA analyst Garrett Nelson said in an investor note. GM expects the fourth quarter will be negatively affected by fewer truck deliveries as it prepares to launch redesigned versions of its Chevrolet Silverado and GMC Sierra, its biggest money makers. STOCK BUYBACK SHOWS CONFIDENCE IN '27 GM said commodity inflation, including higher expenses for logistics and computer chips, would total about $2 billion this year, the high end of its previous forecast. GM said it expects gross tariff costs will hit the lower end of a $2.5 billion to $3.5 billion forecast. For next year, the company said "the path forward is more challenging," but reiterated that it expects results to be better, assuming continued strong consumer demand and a moderating of cost pressures on commodities and logistics. "The consumer has held up remarkably well. We should continue to watch it," GM CFO Paul Jacobson told analysts on the company’s conference call. "We haven't seen anything that indicates any weakness." But he said costs rose sharply over the last two months, specifically for steel, aluminum and logistics. He added that if commodity expenses don’t ease from recent levels, they could weigh on GM’s bottom line by $2 billion next year. JP Morgan said investors "are likely to question conviction for now" because of rising costs and uncertainty over whether the company can sustain its rich sales mix of pricey trucks. MORE TRUCKS, FEWER EVS BOOST PROFITS GM's board approved a multi-year, $20 billion stock buyback program. GM has bought back about $29.5 billion of its own shares since 2023, driving down its overall share count to help its per-share profit results. In the third quarter, it sold a higher mix of large pickup trucks and fewer electric vehicles, which helped the bottom line. The company has been pulling back on sales of EVs, which historically have lost money, following the Trump administration’s withdrawal of support for them. CFRA’s Nelson noted that GM has lost U.S. market share this year and blamed competition from hybrid vehicles, a category in which GM is essentially absent. The automaker in the past decade went all-in on electric vehicles, deciding against offering hybrid vehicles, which now represent more than 15% of US sales. "The company faces a tougher road ahead due to its lack of hybrid offerings," he said. Barra told analysts on a conference call that GM "will have hybrids", although she declined to cite a timeline or other details.

item.title: Hasbro raises annual revenue forecast on strong demand for digital games
item.description: Toymaker Hasbro raised full-year forecast for both overall revenue and its digital gaming business on Tuesday, as its flagship trading card game, "Magic: The Gathering", powers demand ahead of the crucial holiday season.
item.dc:creator: Anuja Mistry
item.content:encoded: Toymaker Hasbro (HAS.O) raised full-year forecast for both overall revenue and its digital gaming business on Tuesday, as its flagship trading card game, "Magic: The Gathering", powers demand ahead of the crucial holiday season. The Play-Doh maker has posted seven straight quarters of gains in digital gaming, which also includes Monopoly Go!, while stronger sales of collectibles linked to Marvel, K-Pop Demon Hunters and Transformers boosted demand for traditional toys. Its shares were up 5%. The Wizards of the Coast and Digital Gaming segment, the company's second-largest revenue generator, grew 31% during the third quarter. Revenue from the consumer products segment rose 4%. Quarterly revenue from "Magic: The Gathering" gaming franchise topped $600 million for the first time, up 34% from a year earlier, fueled by premiere sets — The Hobbit and Reality Fracture. Company executives now expect annual revenue in this segment to grow between 16% and 18%, versus the previous forecast of low double-digit range. "Hasbro's continued momentum is a sign that great play and collectible experiences remain top of mind for American consumers" despite inflationary pressures, said James Zahn, editor-in-chief at the Toy Book magazine. Hasbro expects fiscal 2026 revenue to grow in the range of 7% to 9% on constant currency basis, compared with its prior forecast a 5% to 7% rise. "We are continuing to see a pretty resilient consumer," Chief Financial Officer Gina Goetter said on a post-earnings call, adding the company enters the holiday season in good shape operationally. Hasbro has benefited from strategic partnerships and its investments in digital gaming and product innovation, while rival Mattel (MAT.O) faces investor pressure to better monetize its intellectual property. Quarterly revenue of Hasbro, which also doubled its share repurchase target for the year to about $400 million, stood at $1.60 billion. That beat analysts' average estimate of $1.48 billion, according to data compiled by LSEG. Adjusted profit per share of $2.90 also beat the estimate of $1.86. The company's results included about $55 million of tariff refunds.

BERLIN, Oct 20 : Germany's far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) said on Tuesday that it was investigating the online publication of emails stolen by unknown hackers during a cyberattack last month. An AfD spokesperson said hackers had targeted a hosting service provider used by the party and apparently copied data from a small number of email accounts, most of which had not been used for years.  "The recent online publication of what is presumably a portion of this data is currently being investigated," the spokesperson said. "A preliminary assessment can only be provided once this investigation has been concluded." The spokesperson did not say how much data was stolen.

The statement followed a report by Bild newspaper saying over 420,000 emails linked to the party had been published online.  According to Bild, the material included emails sent by party figures such as co-leader Alice Weidel as well as bank statements, academic certificates and membership lists. The website hosting the material was offline by Tuesday afternoon, but archived versions showed a trove of 281 gigabytes of data under the headline "The party's own records, unedited". The leak comes as the AfD, which has topped national opinion polls and made gains in recent state elections, faces calls from some politicians and civil society groups for it to be banned.  They argue the party threatens Germany's democratic constitutional order, an accusation the AfD rejects as politically motivated.

item.title: Wall Street gains as healthcare stocks rally, oil prices fall
item.description: Wall Street's main indexes climbed on Tuesday as healthcare stocks hit a record high and easing oil prices boosted investor sentiment, while markets continued to stabilize following last week's technology-led selloff.
item.dc:creator: Tharuniyaa Lakshmi, Ragini Mathur
item.content:encoded: Wall Street's main indexes climbed on Tuesday as healthcare stocks hit a record high and easing oil prices boosted investor sentiment, while markets continued to stabilize following last week's technology-led selloff. Brent crude was trading 1.3% lower, reversing course after touching a near five-month high earlier in the day. Most S&P 500 constituents gained, with healthcare (.SPXHC) and financials (.SPSY) rising 1.8% and 1%, respectively. Energy led the losses, while an about 2% decline in Meta Platforms (META.O) pulled the communication services (.SPLRCL) sector down. The market extended Monday's rebound, when the S&P 500 (.SPX) and Nasdaq (.IXIC) climbed as investors bought the dip in technology stocks after last week's sharp selloff, fueled in part by concerns over CoreWeave's (CRWV.O) debt load and the cost of financing the AI buildout. AI-related shares were flat to higher on Tuesday, after showing weakness in premarket trading. CoreWeave was last up 1.6%, while chip gauge Philadelphia Semiconductor index (.SOX) rose 0.4%. "You're seeing some strength in some high-value stocks and the Dow, and so that's helping to sort of lift the overall index," said Robert Pavlik, senior portfolio manager at Dakota Wealth. "Concerns about what's going on as far as semiconductors, that's still there and AI-related names are down, but for the most part, the rest of the market is seeing a bit of a nice rebound." Elsewhere, shares of South Korean AI infrastructure company Elice Group (0158S0.KQ) [USN:L1N466008 TEXT:"tumbled nearly 30% in their market debut"], slipping below their IPO price after the company raised 201.1 billion won ($151.12 million) in its offering. At 10:31 a.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 617.62 points, or 1.22%, to 52,599.29. The S&P 500 (.SPX) gained 53.99 points, or 0.70%, to 7,744.72, while the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) added 154.58 points, or 0.59%, to 26,585.47. Investors are now watching this week's corporate earnings for clues on whether companies can maintain strong growth in the face of mounting macroeconomic risks. Quarterly results from SpaceX (SPCX.O) and Netflix (NFLX.O) are due after the market close on Tuesday, while heavyweights Meta Platforms (META.O) and Tesla (TSLA.O) are scheduled to report on Wednesday. Steel Dynamics (STLD.O) fell 1% after the [USN:L4N4651KV TEXT:"steelmaker missed"] third-quarter profit estimates. General Motors (GM.N) shares dropped 5.3% after the automaker forecast its annual earnings below [USN:L6N4660PI TEXT:"analysts' expectations"]. 3M (MMM.N) gained 5.3% after the [USN:L4N4651MW TEXT:"company said"] it was expanding its data-center partnership with Amazon (AMZN.O) , and issued a warrant to an Amazon subsidiary to purchase 3M common stock worth over $521 million. The industrial conglomerate also raised its full-year profit forecast on Tuesday. Credit reporting firm Equifax (EFX.N) jumped 9.6% after it reported third-quarter profit above analysts' estimates. Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 3.55-to-1 ratio on the NYSE and by 3.45-to-1 on the Nasdaq. The S&P 500 posted 21 new 52-week highs and one new low, while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 26 new highs and 183 new lows.

item.title: Aerospace and military contractors raise 2026 profit forecasts
item.description: Northrop Grumman and RTX raised their annual profit forecasts on Tuesday, helped by robust demand from military programs that pushed their backlogs to record levels.
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Singh, Aatreyee Dasgupta, Mike Stone
item.content:encoded: Northrop Grumman (NOC.N) and RTX (RTX.N) raised their annual profit forecasts on Tuesday, helped by robust demand from military programs that pushed their backlogs to record levels. Sustained demand for commercial aerospace services also fueled growth, both at [USN:L4N4660T1 TEXT:"RTX"] and rival engine maker [USN:L4N4660OA TEXT:"GE Aerospace"] (GE.N) , which lifted its full-year forecast for a second time this year. Northrop shares jumped by 7.2% in early trading and RTX gained 2.4% while GE Aerospace lost 4.9% on lower than expected implied fourth-quarter earnings. GEOPOLITICAL BACKDROP BRINGS SUSTAINED MILITARY SPENDING The results add to strong performances among US aerospace and defense contractors, supported by airline maintenance spending, growing demand for aircraft engines and parts and sustained military spending at a time of heightened geopolitical tensions around the globe. Sales at RTX's Raytheon climbed 14%, driven by higher volume in naval programs and land and air defense systems, including Patriot, Standard Missile and Tomahawk. "We continue to see robust global demand for all of our products and services," RTX finance chief Neil Mitchill told Reuters on Tuesday, adding that the company had "another record backlog" of $340 billion, up 36% from a year ago. [USN:L4N4660MP TEXT:"Northrop"], which makes the B-21 Raider bomber and parts for F-35 fighter jets, registered a similar 14% sales increase at its Aeronautics Systems unit, which benefited from increased B-21 sales and higher F-35 production. The company secured $16.4 billion in new contracts during the quarter, with its orders growing at 1.5 times its billings, driven by strong demand across programs including Sentinel, the F-35, Virginia-class submarines and certain classified programs. Northrop's backlog rose to a record $109.6 billion by September 30. Similarly, RTX chalked up $81 billion in new commercial and defense awards, pushing its backlog to a record $340 billion. Beyond the military sphere, RTX was helped by airline maintenance spending and growing demand for its Pratt & Whitney aircraft engines and parts even as surging fuel costs squeeze airline profits. GE Aerospace registered similarly firm demand, with revenue at its commercial engines and services business rising more than a fifth to $10.34 billion. It acknowledged, however, that prolonged high fuel prices could lead airlines to reduce flying, weakening demand for engine repairs, spare parts and spare engines. Northrop now expects full-year 2026 adjusted profit per share in the range of $29.35 to $29.75, up from a previous forecast of between $28.60 and $29.10. RTX now forecasts 2026 adjusted earnings per share of $7.65 to $7.75, up from its previous projection of $7.10 to $7.25. It also raised its sales forecast range to between $97 billion and $97.5 billion, from $95 billion to $96 billion. GE Aerospace now expects adjusted earnings of $8.00 to $8.10 per share in 2026, up from its previous forecast of $7.65 to $7.85 and above analyst expectations of $7.92, according to data compiled by LSEG.

item.title: Britain seeks to break Apple's grip on contactless payments
item.description: Britain's competition regulator said on Tuesday it was seeking to loosen Apple's grip on contactless payments by proposing that the company lower fees and remove technical barriers, helping rival services compete with Apple Pay.
item.dc:creator: Paul Sandle
item.content:encoded: Britain's competition regulator said on Tuesday it was seeking to loosen Apple's grip on contactless payments by proposing that the company lower fees and remove technical barriers, helping rival services compete with Apple Pay. The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) said its proposals would result in "substantially lower access fees" and easier access to Apple's contactless technology. The measures are less onerous than those imposed by the European Union in 2024, which included free access for third-party developers. Companies including PayPal, Klarna, Curve and BBVA have since launched alternative payment apps, the CMA said. 'HIGH FEES, STRICT TERMS' The EU commitments require Apple to give wallet developers access to the iPhone's NFC chip using host card emulation (HCE), allowing third-party apps to process contactless payments without going through Apple Pay or Apple Wallet. The CMA's proposals would give developers access to HCE in addition to Apple's existing secure element (SE) technology. The regulator can impose requirements on Apple after designating it and Google as having strategic market status in smartphones last year. Contactless payments account for 39% of all payments, compared with 3% a decade ago, the CMA said. More than 60% of adults use a digital wallet, with Apple Wallet the most popular in Britain. CMA Chief Executive Sarah Cardell said the proposals would boost innovation, consumer choice and Britain's fintech sector. "We have heard that high fees, strict terms, and technical restrictions relating to Apple's contactless technology make it too difficult for challengers to innovate and compete," she said. The CMA is consulting on the proposals until November 17, before making a final decision. Digital bank Revolut welcomed the proposals, saying access to NFC technology through HCE was critical. "The CMA's direction creates a real opportunity for UK fintechs to compete on an equal footing with Big Tech," said Revolut's chief commercial officer, David Tirado. Apple said developers could already offer contactless payments through its NFC technology and secure element, which stores sensitive information such as card credentials and cryptographic keys. It said this enabled services including in-store payments, transit passes and event tickets while protecting users' data. "We do not believe the CMA should require Apple to adopt an approach with lower privacy and security protections," an Apple spokesperson said. "We will continue to engage constructively to reach an outcome that is in the best interest of our users."

Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 ２０日 ロイター] - 赤沢亮正経済産業相は２０日の閣議後会見で、欧州連合（ＥＵ）が検討する欧州製電気自動車（ＥＶ）の優遇措置案について、「日本を念頭に置いて排除するものではない」との趣旨の説明をしているとした上で、「目的と手段が合っていないなというのが正直なところだ」と苦言を呈した。

赤沢経産相は、日本製を優遇対象外とする最終決定が出されれば「影響が小さいとはとても言えない」と指摘。日本企業が不利益を被ることがないよう懸念を伝え、日本製はＥＵ製と同等とみなすよう申し入れているという。

Cloud computing service provider CoreWeave Inc.’s bonds dropped this month, sending yields on its 2032 notes as high as 15%. Yields for junk and investment-grade debt reached the highest since 2025 and 2023, respectively. The implication is that the cost of corporate credit, a key channel through which central banks tap the economy’s brakes to cool inflation, may start to weigh on growth.

item.content:encoded:

Why US satellites are so crucial to Ukraine’s defence, and why Kyiv can’t look to Europe for help

Kyiv’s reliance on US tech reemerged as a vulnerability mid-October. Around the same time, sudden restrictions were reported on SpaceX Starlink satellite services used by Ukraine.

Gerry Doyle

20 October, 2026 03:30 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

A model of a Gen4 ICEYE satellite at the companys headquarters in Espoo, Finland.

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

Ukraine’s defense against Russian attacks depends heavily on US satellites, not only for warning of incoming missiles but also for the communications that keep drones and frontline forces operating.

European nations are trying to catch up with the US in space-based intelligence and connectivity, but still lack many crucial capabilities that underpin Ukrainian combat operations and missile-defense systems.

Kyiv’s reliance on American technology and support reemerged as a vulnerability in mid-October, when President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine had not received the usual warning from allies of ballistic missile launches before a deadly attack on the country. Around the same time, sudden restrictions were reported on SpaceX Starlink satellite services used by Ukrainian forces.

Show Full Article

Why are US satellites so important for Ukraine?

Starlink — the low-earth orbit commercial satellite communication network established by Elon Musk’s SpaceX — and its military version, Starshield, have come to underpin the Ukrainian armed forces’ command infrastructure after terrestrial communications were badly damaged by Russian strikes early in the war. The ground terminals allow pilots of Ukrainian interceptor drones and mid-range strike drones to control the machines, while the network also allows ground forces to coordinate supplies and movements along the front line.

US military satellites are also vital for Ukraine’s defense against Russian missiles and drones.

No country beside the US can offer near-constant space-based imaging of Europe. Its numerous and powerful spy satellites can provide high-quality images, including video. Via the Space Based Infrared System, or SBIRS, the US also has satellites in geosynchronous orbit, which keeps them over one spot on earth. These are the backbone of US early warning for missiles anywhere on Earth, and there is no equivalent in Europe. The satellites allow for real-time tracking of cruise missiles and other low-flying weapons that might escape detection by ground radar until it’s too late to stop them. This is especially helpful for a military, such as Ukraine’s, that relies on drones, aircraft cannons and other low-tech methods of destroying swarms of mass-produced projectiles.

SBIRS can also detect the launch plumes of ballistic missiles. These missiles travel much faster and higher than other airborne weapons, making them harder to deal with. Knowing when a ballistic missile is fired, its speed and direction is vital for Ukraine’s air-raid warning systems. (An alert — even one that comes a minute or two ahead of the impact — can save lives by giving civilians time to take cover).

That capability also gives Ukraine’s armed forces a greater chance of intercepting and destroying the inbound weapons. It can be harder to knock out a missile at longer range. But a miss at long range still allows time for another shot. If an incoming missile is only noticed at the last minute, a miss at close range blows the final chance to foil a potentially devastating attack.

How were these capabilities disrupted recently?

Ukrainian officials said the US government did not send early warning alerts ahead of some recent Russian ballistic missile attacks on the country.

Ukraine also complained that drones equipped with Starlink terminals were losing connectivity when traveling at speeds above 161 kilometers (100 miles) per hour in Ukraine. The drones often need to travel faster than this to intercept an incoming Russian drone traveling at 400 kilometers per hour, and the restrictions have disrupted drone interceptions and mid-range strikes.

Asked who ordered the change, President Zelenskyy pointed to “the authorities, the White House,” citing “sources” he didn’t identify. A senior US official has said Trump didn’t order any limitations.

How does Europe use its satellites to help Ukraine?

Europe’s militaries have a variety of earth-observation satellites that help Ukrainian forces locate Russian troops, tanks, artillery and military installations and identify ammunition depots, airfields and missile-launch facilities. The Ukrainian military can use that information to strike at those facilities.

Finland’s ICEYE synthetic-aperture radar satellites can operate at night and see through cloud cover, smoke and haze. French satellite sensors detect thermal radiation and identify human activity that conventional cameras can easily miss.

Germany has paid commercial satellite companies such as US-based Planet Labs for high-resolution imagery for Ukraine, including inside Russian territory. This can provide data for targeting and spotting Russian military movement over time — potentially crucial intelligence that could thwart an attempted attack.

When might Europe close the intelligence gap?

Europe is under heavy pressure to stop relying on the US for its own defense, and military budgets in the region are growing again for the first time since the Cold War. A chunk of that new spending is going toward “strategic enablers” — communications and other systems that have an outsized impact on warfare despite not being weapons. European nations are racing to put more satellites in orbit and get more surveillance aircraft in the air.

The European Union has begun launching the first of nearly 350 Iris2 secure communications satellites. ICEYE recently signed a deal with Nokia to develop a secure communications constellation for European defense and security. Airbus SE has for decades built satellites, and German defense giant Rheinmetall AG has also entered the game, including through a partnership with ICEYE.

The pace of the rollout is limited, however, as the region does not have enough rockets with the power to launch heavy military satellites into orbit. Europe’s only sovereign heavy rocket booster is Ariane 6, which launches about 10 times a year from Kourou in French Guyana on the northern coast of South America. And European governments want to avoid using SpaceX as they prefer to find their own way into orbit.

So could Europe eventually match the US for space-based intelligence?

No existing or currently planned European service could match the scale and capability of Starlink. The closest existing European equivalent is OneWeb, a system of around 600 satellites operated by France’s Eutelsat. Starlink satellites orbit at an altitude of around 550 km, around half that of OneWeb’s network. This makes for shorter signal transmission delays — a crucial factor with time-critical military systems. The 10,000-satellite Starlink network also offers greater data capacity and better ground coverage, and its terminals are smaller so they can be mounted more easily on drones.

When it comes to military observation satellites, there’s no European plan to match the capability of US SBIRS. The US has nearly 250 military satellites in orbit, compared with about 150 for China and about 100 for Russia. Many more are considered dual-use.

Europe as a whole has about 50.

Besides imagery, US satellites can intercept communications and other transmissions — so-called “signals intelligence” that can also be used on the battlefield.

The US Space Force also announced in September that it had placed an operational weapon in orbit, although officials declined to say what sort of system it was.

–With assistance from Michael Nienaber and Volodymyr Verbianyi.

item.title: Colombian Congress approves budget allocations, cuts funding to peace deal
item.description: Colombian lawmakers approved spending distributions for next year's 634.9 trillion pesos ($201.14 billion) budget early on Tuesday, trimming spending linked to a 10-year-old peace agreement and boosting debt service payments.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Colombian lawmakers approved spending distributions for next year's 634.9 trillion pesos ($201.14 billion) budget early on Tuesday, trimming spending linked to a 10-year-old peace agreement and boosting debt service payments. The budget, which projects a 2027 fiscal deficit of 9.4% of gross domestic product, is a significant increase from the 555.8 trillion peso budget for this year. The bill allocates 141 trillion pesos, about $45 billion for debt repayment next year, up from about $30 billion allocated in 2026. Neither congress nor the finance ministry had published a complete breakdown of the approved budget by morning on Tuesday and a congressional source told Reuters a final version could take days, as some modifications were approved by only one of the chambers. The bigger budget comes as Colombia, Latin America's fourth-largest economy, struggles to put its public accounts in order. Public debt is expected to rise this year and next, moving the country further from regaining the investment-grade rating it lost in 2021. The government of new right-wing President Abelardo De La Espriella had promised to trim remaining spending for this year and said it plans to propose a 'Rescue Law' to Congress to cut 2027 spending and reduce the fiscal deficit to 7.2% of GDP. Lawmakers in the lower house approved the bill with 112 votes in favor and only one against it, while in the Senate it passed with 57 votes in favor and one against. Lawmakers had until Tuesday night to pass the budget before it would be possible for the government to put it through via decree. "Thank you all for giving us this vote of confidence. We are going to succeed in getting the country out of this very complex economic situation," Finance Minister Miguel Gomez said after the Senate passed the bill late on Monday night. SPENDING CUTS The budget cuts funds for the Special Jurisdiction for Peace (JEP) - the court created under a 2016 peace deal with the former Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) guerrillas to try rebel leaders and ex-soldiers for war crimes - by some 181 billion pesos, the finance ministry said in a statement, and reassigns that money to the defense ministry. The cut amounts to 23% of the court's budget, an even deeper reduction than had been previously expected. Several lawmakers said the budget for the Search Unit for Disappeared People (UBPD), created under the peace deal to look for at least 137,000 people who vanished during the ongoing armed conflict, had also been cut, but there were not yet final figures showing by how much. The two entities and advocates have said cuts will [USN:L6N45R12F TEXT:"limit investigations and trials"] into human rights violations, as well as exhumations and identifications of the disappeared. ($1 = 3,156.50 Colombian pesos)

item.content:encoded:
独ＺＥＷ景気期待指数、10月28.1で予想下回る　6カ月ぶりに低下 10/20 18:52 配信

Linda Pasquini

[ベルリン ２０日 ロイター] - 欧州経済研究センター（ＺＥＷ）が２０日発表した１０月のドイツ景気期待指数は２８．１で予想以上に低下した。エネルギー価格の高止まりが個人消費や投資の重荷となり、６カ月ぶりの低下となった。

ロイターがまとめたアナリスト予想は３０、前月は３４．７だった。

ＺＥＷのアヒム・ワムバッハ所長は「ドイツ経済は緩やかに停滞から抜け出しつつあるが、回復は自律的なものではない」と指摘。エネルギー価格の高止まりで個人消費と投資が引き続き低迷しており、実質所得を圧迫し生産コストを押し上げ、インフレの高止まりが長引いているとした。

先に発表された９月の生産者物価は、エネルギー価格の上昇で３年半ぶりの大幅な伸びとなった。原油・天然ガス価格の上昇が景気回復を鈍らせている。ワムバッハ氏は、ドイツ経済は緩やかに停滞から抜け出しつつあるものの、自律的な回復はなものではないと指摘した。

連立与党は、極右政党「ドイツのための選択肢（ＡｆＤ）」の台頭で圧力が強まっている。１２日のバス労働相の辞任も不透明感を強めた。

ドイツ銀行リサーチのエコノミスト、フェリシタス・ヘンツェ氏は「最近の政治動向は、夏に発表された改革計画の迅速な実施を巡る不透明感を強めたとみられる」と述べた。

現況指数はマイナス３５．９で９月のマイナス４７．１から改善、改善幅は予想を上回った。

ドイツ経済省は今月、イラン戦争による経済への悪影響は懸念していたほどではないとして、２０２６年と２７年の経済成長率見通しを引き上げた。

ＶＰバンクのチーフエコノミスト、トーマス・ギッツェル氏は「受注残が高水準にあるため、産業界は当面は生産を増やすことができる。これが経済見通しの改善の理由でもある」と述べた。

国内経済は第２・四半期に０．３％成長した。ギッツェル氏は「予想外に底堅かった」上半期が２６年の成長を支えるはずだと指摘。第３・四半期はほとんど成長しなかったとみられるが、ＺＥＷ調査は第４・四半期にも新たな大きな成長の勢いは生じないことを示していると述べた。

調査は１０月１２─１９日に実施、アナリストと機関投資家１７８人の回答に基づく。

Zelenskyy travels to Oslo for new peace talks as pressure mounts from US to reach a deal with Russia

US envoy Steve Witkoff is expected in Oslo to take part in the talks with Norwegian Pm Jonas Gahr Støre and Finland’s President Alexander Stubb. Jared Kushner will take part online.

Olesia Safronova

20 October, 2026 03:19 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

Volodymyr Zelenskyy in London on Oct. 14. Photographer: Betty Laura Zapata/Bloomberg

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is traveling to Norway for new peace talks as US pressure mounts for concessions from Kyiv to reach a deal with Russia.

US envoy Steve Witkoff is expected in Oslo to take part in the talks on Tuesday with Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Finland’s President Alexander Stubb, according to a government statement in Norway. Another US envoy, Jared Kushner, will take part online in the talks, the statement said.

The meeting’s being held amid escalating tensions between Zelenskyy and Donald Trump. The American president reiterated criticism of the Ukrainian leader on Monday after officials in Kyiv said they suspect the US is intermittently restricting intelligence sharing despite denials from Washington, allowing Russian missiles to strike Ukraine without warning.

Show Full Article

Zelenskyy “doesn’t know what he’s talking about” and should have settled the war a long time ago, Trump told reporters. “We’ve given a lot to Ukraine. They’ve given us nothing.”

Relations between Trump and Zelenskyy have soured since the US announced a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin this month for diesel supplies to American and global markets as the White House strives to cut surging fuel prices ahead of Nov. 3 midterm elections.

Trump followed that up by deferring sweeping new sanctions targeting Russian energy sales. That sparked criticism from lawmakers including in his own Republican party that he was helping Russia to continue financing the war that Putin started in February 2022.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said in an interview with Bloomberg on Monday that Putin is seeking not only to defeat Ukraine, but to also undermine democracy in Europe. The key condition in the war was Ukraine’s territorial integrity “and that is not to dispute,” he said.

“I’m trying to convince Donald Trump each time I’m meeting him that this should be in his own interest,” Merz said. “A stable Europe, European continent, European Union as a partner in the world is something which is worthwhile for the Americans as well.”

The Ukrainian leader spoke by video call with Witkoff and Kushner, who is Trump’s son-in-law, on Sunday to discuss the war and possibilities for new talks. Zelenskyy said in a Bloomberg News interview on Sunday that the US side also planned to meet with Putin.

A Russian strike involving 16 ballistic missiles overnight on Sunday and Monday was the third time in the same week in which Ukraine was left without the usual advance warning it receives from US intelligence about incoming attacks. Ukraine has also accused the US of restricting access to SpaceX’s Starshield satellite technology.

How US Satellites Became Crucial to Ukraine’s Defense: Explainer

Zelenskyy said Tuesday he held “constructive” talks with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio about ballistic missile interceptors, early warning on attacks and the situation with Starshield “which needs to be restored.” They agreed to be in contact soon for an update, he said in a post on social media.

US officials have rebuffed accusations of any slowdown in intelligence to Ukraine. Trump last week said he didn’t order limitations on Ukraine’s access to Starshield.

Trump said Monday that “somebody else” instead of Zelenskyy should negotiate on behalf of Ukraine. He told reporters that “Russia frankly has been fine on Ukraine — they haven’t been doing much.”

(Updates with German chancellor in the seventh, eighth paragraphs. An earlier version of this story corrected the date to Tuesday in what is now the 11th paragraph.)

FAST

Oct 20 : Amazon plans to invest more than €16 billion (about $18 billion) in Germany in 2027, the company said on Tuesday, to expand its cloud computing, AI, satellite internet and media businesses. The investment is the e-commerce giant's latest move to grow its European operations as it races to expand cloud infrastructure across the region amid surging demand for AI services and growing competition among technology firms. The package, announced at the Invest in Germany Summit in Berlin, adds to more than €100 billion Amazon says it has invested in the country since 2010. The latest investment includes €4.8 billion to expand Amazon Web Services' Frankfurt cloud region and AI infrastructure.

Amazon also plans to open a second robotics and AI research lab in Berlin. Tuesday's commitment follows a €10 billion investment announced in June 2024 to expand its cloud infrastructure and logistics network in Germany, including €8.8 billion for AWS data centres. item.title: ＡＢＢ第3四半期、受注高が過去最高 データセンター向け好調
item.description:
John Revill
[チューリヒ ２０日 ロイター] - スイスのエンジニアリング大手ＡＢＢは２０日、人工知能（Ａ...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＡＢＢ第3四半期、受注高が過去最高　データセンター向け好調 10/20 18:28 配信

スイスのエンジニアリング大手ＡＢＢのロゴ。2024年3月26日、パリ近郊で撮影。 REUTERS/Benoit Tessier

John Revill

[チューリヒ ２０日 ロイター] - スイスのエンジニアリング大手ＡＢＢは２０日、人工知能（ＡＩ）向けデータセンターへの投資ブームを背景に、第３・四半期の受注高が４０％増の１２０億ドルと、過去最高を記録したと発表した。

受注を大きく押し上げたのは、データセンターで使われる配電・冷却システムなどへの旺盛な需要だった。データセンター向けの受注は２倍超に増えた。

ＡＢＢは受注増を受け、通期見通しを小幅に引き上げた。比較可能ベースの売上高伸び率の予想を「１０％台前半」とした。従来は「１０％台の低い水準から１０％台前半」としていた。

第３・四半期の売上高は１４％増の９７億ドルだった。同社が集計したアナリスト予想の９７億４０００万ドルをわずかに下回った。営業ベースのＥＢＩＴＡ（利払い・税引き・無形資産償却前利益）は２４％増の２０億３０００万ドルと、アナリスト予想の２０億ドルをわずかに上回った。

ＡＢＢは同日、三菱電機との低圧配電事業の合弁会社の株式５１％を４億９５００万ドルで取得すると発表した。

ＡＢＢのモーテン・ウィーロッド最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は「今回の取引により、世界有数の電化市場である日本で、低圧機器市場の首位に立つことになる。国内のデータセンター整備を含め、電力分野の幅広い潮流から恩恵を受けられる」と述べた。「アジア太平洋地域での事業拡大にも道が開ける」とした。

item.title: コアウィーブ売り、グローバル銀行のリスク限定的＝ＪＰモルガン
item.description:
Siddarth S
[２０日 ロイター] - ＪＰモルガンは２０日、エヌビディアが支援するクラウド企業コアウィーブの...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
コアウィーブ売り、グローバル銀行のリスク限定的＝ＪＰモルガン 10/20 18:18 配信

コアウィーブのロゴが表示された画面。2026年7月20日撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration/File Photo

Siddarth S

[２０日 ロイター] - ＪＰモルガンは２０日、エヌビディアが支援するクラウド企業コアウィーブの株式と債券が先週急落したことを受け、大半のグローバル銀行について同社へのエクスポージャーは限定的との評価を示した。

複数の米大手投資銀行や日本の三菱ＵＦＪフィナンシャル・グループ（ＭＵＦＧ）はコアウィーブに対して約１０億─３０億ドルのエクスポージャーを抱えている可能性がある一方、欧州やアジアのプレーヤーの大部分は５億ドル未満にとどまっているという。

ＪＰモルガンによると、その多くは「遅延引き出しタームローン」を通じて行われており、これらは主に特別目的事業体（ＳＰＶ）を通じて保有され、プロジェクトがマイルストーンを達成するにつれて資金が解放される仕組みとなっている。

アナリストらはリポートで「融資銀行の観点から見て、コアウィーブに対する銀行のエクスポージャーは適切に管理されており、担保も非常に充実している」と指摘。各行がＡＩ（人工知能）投資サイクルに対するエクスポージャーについて開示を限定しているため、この推定値は「簡略化された仮定」に基づいていると述べた。

ＪＰモルガンはコアウィーブに対し「オーバーウエート」の投資判断を付与しており、２０２７年末時点の目標株価を１２５ドルとしている。

各行が直面する主なリスクは、ＡＩインフラへの先行投資と、長期的に得られる収益とのミスマッチにあると指摘し、コアウィーブのフリーキャッシュフローは３０年までマイナスが続くと予想していると付け加えた。

Google Cloud services largely back up in UK; Revolut services remain disrupted in Singapore

All 27 services listed on Revolut's Singapore status page were partially unavailable, including card payments, ATM withdrawals and currency exchange.

A pedestrian walks past the Google offices in London, Britain, August 14, 2025. REUTERS/Suzanne Plunkett

20 Oct 2026 05:11PM (Updated: 20 Oct 2026 10:58PM)

FAST

LONDON: A power outage at a Google Cloud data centre near London caused serious failures to services on Tuesday, leading to widespread disruptions for several UK banks. Google said in a service health update that most services had returned to normal by 1210 GMT (8.10pm Singapore time), six hours after the incident began. "We are seeing the recovery of services for most workloads in europe-west2," the US tech giant said, referring to its London data centre. Google said its cloud services suffered an outage "due to a power event", in an incident that began at 0608 GMT.
