Acceleration in fourth-quarter growth was led by the Digital Scalers segment, CEO Octave Klaba told Reuters, following the reorganisation of the company's offering since his return a year ago. Digital Scalers, which serves clients spending more than €2,000 a month, posted comparable revenue growth of 12.4 per cent to €359.1 million and made up 31 per cent of the company's sales. Public cloud revenue rose 18.9 per cent to €255.1 million. Klaba said the year had been one of discipline and OVHcloud had "returned to its fundamentals". Levered free cash flow reached €24.7 million, against an outflow of €27.0 million a year ago. Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation rose 9.7 per cent to €480.5 million, resulting in a margin of 42.0 per cent. For fiscal 2027, it aims to raise the margin to above 42.5 per cent. Net debt stood at €1.16 billion, or 2.7 times its adjusted EBITDA, compared with 2.9x at the end of the previous fiscal year. The company has €255 million in available liquidity and no significant debt repayment due before fiscal 2030, it said. ($1 = 0.8904 euros)

Source: Reuters

item.description:
Shiho Tanaka
[東京 ２０日 ロイター] - 三菱電機は２０日、配電制御機器事業を分割し、スイスの電力...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
三菱電機、ＡＢＢと配電制御事業で合弁　28年3月期に利益900億円 10/20 14:03 配信

写真は三菱電機のロゴ。2026年8月、都内で撮影。REUTERS/Kentaro Okasaka

Shiho Tanaka

[東京 ２０日 ロイター] - 三菱電機は２０日、配電制御機器事業を分割し、スイスの電力・オートメーション大手ＡＢＢの日本法人に新会社株式の５１％を約８２４億円で譲渡して合弁会社を設立すると発表した。株式譲渡により、２０２８年３月期連結決算において関連する利益約９００億円を計上する見込み。

１２月１日に準備会社を設立し、２７年１０月１日を効力発生日として吸収分割により事業を新会社へ承継させる。新会社への出資比率はＡＢＢが５１％、三菱電機が４９％となる予定。

配電制御機器とは発電所から供給される電力を分配・制御するための配電盤や遮断器などで、三菱電機は製造や販売を手がけている。国内では高い市場シェアを有する一方、海外では電化の普及に伴う需要増と競争激化が見込まれており、ＡＢＢとの共同運営が必要と判断した。

item.description: [２０日 ロイター] - 資源大手ＢＨＰグループが２０日発表した２０２７年度第１・四半期（７─９月）の銅生産量は４０万...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＢＨＰ、7─9月銅生産が前年比19％減　チリ鉱山の一時操業停止影響 10/20 13:58 配信

ＢＨＰのエスコンディダ鉱山で、採掘現場の前に立つ作業員ら。2008年3月、チリ北部のアントファガスタで撮影。REUTERS/Ivan Alvarado

[２０日 ロイター] - 資源大手ＢＨＰグループが２０日発表した２０２７年度第１・四半期（７─９月）の銅生産量は４０万０７００トンで、前年同期の４９万４０００トンから１９％減少した。チリの主力鉱山エスコンディーダでの悪天候や死亡事故に伴う操業停止が響いた。

エスコンディーダ鉱山では９月下旬、保守作業中の作業員が死亡する事故が発生し、一時操業を停止した。また、オーストラリア南部のカラパティーナ銅山でも坑内コンベアベルトの故障により数週間にわたり生産が妨げられた。

第１・四半期の銅生産量は、ビジブル・アルファ集計の市場予想４２万３６００トンも下回った。

銅は今年、人工知能（ＡＩ）向けデータセンター需要の拡大を背景に、ＢＨＰの最大の利益源となっている。

一方ウエスタンオーストラリア州の鉄鉱石事業の第１・四半期生産量は７１９０万トンと、前年同期の７０２０万トンをやや上回った。ＢＨＰは２８年度末までに年産３億０５００万トン体制への増産を進めている。

第１・四半期の鉄鉱石の平均実現価格は、前年同期比９％下落の１湿潤トン当たり７６．２７ドルだった。

ＢＨＰは、全事業における通期生産見通しは据え置き、オリンピックダム鉱山の銅資源量推計を２００万トン引き上げた。現在の生産水準で約９年分の追加生産に相当するという。

item.title: アマゾン、独自ＡＩ半導体普及に向け新ソフト導入へ エヌビディア優位に対抗
item.description:
Stephen Nellis
[サンフランシスコ １９日 ロイター] - 米アマゾン・ドット・コムは、独自開発した人工...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
アマゾン、独自ＡＩ半導体普及に向け新ソフト導入へ　エヌビディア優位に対抗 10/20 13:38 配信

写真は人工知能（ＡＩ）のイメージ。10月19日に撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

Stephen Nellis

[サンフランシスコ １９日 ロイター] - 米アマゾン・ドット・コムは、独自開発した人工知能（ＡＩ）半導体上で、最も広く使われているＡＩ開発フレームワーク「PyTorch」で書かれたコードをほぼ無修正で実行できる新たなソフトウエアを導入する。ＡＩコンピューティング市場で圧倒的な地位を築くエヌビディア の競争上の優位を切り崩すのが狙い。

アマゾンの半導体部門アンナプルナ・ラボによると、新ソフト「TorchNeuron」を使えば、開発者は設定を１カ所変更するだけで、PyTorchで書かれたコードをアマゾンのＡＩ半導体「Trainium」上で実行できる。コードを書き直す必要はないという。

アマゾンは１９日にシリコンバレーで開く開発者向け会議で新ソフトを発表する予定。このソフトは無料のオープンソース型として一般公開するという。

PyTorchはメタ・プラットフォームズが管理するオープンソースのフレームワークで、ＡＩ開発者の大半が利用している。エヌビディアは、PyTorchのコードを自社製半導体上で効率よく動作させるソフト開発基盤「CUDA」の開発に１０年余りを費やしてきた。

アンナプルナ・ラボのソフトウエア担当副社長コリン・ブレース氏は今回の取り組みについて、開発者がアマゾン独自の半導体を試すまでに必要な手順を減らすことが目的だと説明。「顧客が現在利用している環境に合わせることが狙いだ」と述べた。

ブレース氏によると、ロボティクス、ワールドモデル（現実世界の挙動を学習・予測するＡＩ）、音声ＡＩなどの分野にまたがる３０社余りの先行顧客がすでに新ソフトを利用している。アマゾンの半導体に切り替えることで大幅なコスト削減につながるという。

item.title: 人民元が4年超ぶり高値、輸出好調と元高の基準値で＝上海外為市場
item.description: [香港 ２０日 ロイター] - 上海外国為替市場の人民元相場は対ドルで４年余りぶりの高値を付けた。中国人民銀行（中央銀...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
人民元が4年超ぶり高値、輸出好調と元高の基準値で＝上海外為市場 10/20 13:37 配信

中国人民元と米ドルの紙幣。22年9月撮影。REUTERS/Florence Lo

[香港 ２０日 ロイター] - 上海外国為替市場の人民元相場は対ドルで４年余りぶりの高値を付けた。中国人民銀行（中央銀行）が基準値（中間値）を元高方向に設定したことに加え、好調な輸出を背景にした企業の決済需要が相場を押し上げた。

オンショア人民元は午前の取引で一時１ドル＝６．６７８９元まで上昇し、２０２２年６月２８日以来の高値を付けた。

オフショア人民元は約０．０５％高の１ドル＝６．６７８７元で取引され、こちらも４年余りぶりの高値となった。

中国の第３・四半期経済成長率は４．５％と、約３年ぶりの低水準だった第２・四半期の４．３％から加速。市場予想を上回った。国内消費が低迷する中でも、輸出と鉱工業生産が引き続き成長をけん引した。

人民銀行は２０日、銀行貸出金利の指標となる最優遇貸出金利（ローンプライムレート、ＬＰＲ）を市場の予想通り１７カ月連続で据え置いた。堅調な国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）統計を受け、政策当局が追加金融緩和を急いでいないことを示した。

格付け会社、中証鵬元のアナリストはリポートで「今回の人民元上昇を最も直接的に支えているのは、貿易部門の好調だ」と指摘した。

人民元の上昇基調が続く中、企業が外貨から元への両替を加速させ、元高の勢いを強めていると説明。元は今後も緩やかに上昇し、年末までに１ドル＝６．６０─６．７０元のレンジで取引されると予想した。

人民銀は市場の取引開始前に、対ドル基準値を１ドル＝６．７２元に設定した。２３年２月２日以来の元高水準となった。ただロイターの推計と比べると３８７ポイントの元安だった。

item.title: 豪ＮＡＢ、コスト削減で2500人削減へ 信用鈍化で
item.description:
Scott Murdoch Rajasik Mukherjee
[シドニー ２０日 ロイター] - 豪大手行ナショナル...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
豪ＮＡＢ、コスト削減で2500人削減へ　信用鈍化で 10/20 13:28 配信

ＮＡＢのロゴ。シドニー市内の支店で25年8月撮影。REUTERS/Hollie Adams

Scott Murdoch　Rajasik Mukherjee

[シドニー ２０日 ロイター] - 豪大手行ナショナル・オーストラリア銀行（ＮＡＢ）は２０日、国内の信用拡大が依然として厳しい状況にある中、業務の簡素化とコスト削減を図るため、来年までに最大２５００人（従業員総数の約６％）を削減すると発表した。

オーストラリア最大の企業向け融資機関であり、住宅ローン分野では第３位のＮＡＢは、年内に最大１５００人のポストを削減すると述べた。

削減の対象は、顧客対応を行う銀行員よりも、法人向け業務に従事する従業員が中心となるという。

また、コンサルタントや契約社員の活用も大幅に削減する計画だ。

アンドリュー・アーバイン最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は声明で、「当社の目標と戦略に変更はない。生産性、リスク管理、業務遂行力を向上させ、よりシンプルで効率的な銀行となる」と述べた。

ＮＡＢの株価はこの日、２．５％近く下落した。

ＮＡＢはまた、金融セクター労働組合との協議を開始すると発表した。同組合幹部のニコール・マクファーソン氏は、人員削減は組織の簡素化にはつながらないと指摘した上で「クリスマスを目前に控えたこの時期に、従業員数の６％を解雇するという破壊的な措置を講じることは恥ずべきことであり、ＮＡＢの経営陣が従業員の実際の生活実態から完全に乖離していることを示している」と批判した。

ＮＡＢはこの大改革により、２７年には、人員削減、配置転換、組織再編にかかる費用として、税引前約３億オーストラリアドル（２億９００万米ドル）の再編費用が発生する見込みだ。

今回の人員削減は、住宅市場の低迷、競争の激化、および運営コストの上昇が収益を圧迫する中、オーストラリアの銀行各社に対する圧力が高まっていた状況を受けて行われたものだ。

ＮＡＢは８月、連邦政府による不動産税改革を受けて、２７年には住宅ローンの伸びが急激に鈍化すると警告していた。同行は、この改革が住宅購入者や投資家からの需要を冷え込ませたと指摘していた。

アーバイン氏は当時、地政学的な不確実性、国内金利の上昇、税制改正が相まって、顧客にとっての課題となっていると述べていた。

ＮＡＢの最新の年次報告書によると、２５年９月３０日時点で、同銀行は世界全体で４万１８８０人を雇用していた。

item.title: ‘It was crazy’: Australian barber hailed as hero after rushing to lawmaker’s rescue
item.description: Australian barber Ricky Jefferies said he ran to assist lawmaker Helen Haines, grabbing a knife from the alleged attacker's pocket and pulling him out of the car.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

‘It was crazy’: Australian barber hailed as hero after rushing to lawmaker’s rescue

Australian barber Ricky Jefferies said he ran to assist lawmaker Helen Haines, grabbing a knife from the alleged attacker's pocket and pulling him out of the car.

Barber Ricky Jefferies speaks to the media a day after tackling a man who attacked Australian politician Helen Haines in the northern regional city of Wangaratta on Oct 20, 2026. (Photo: AFP/William West)

FAST

SYDNEY: Australian barber Ricky Jefferies has been hailed as a hero for running out of his store to detain a man who authorities allege deliberately drove a car into lawmaker Helen Haines in the small town of Wangaratta, an incident that has shocked the country.    Jefferies had just finished haircuts for a young family on Monday (Oct 19) when he said he heard a "loud bang" outside his shop and realised the driver of a Toyota LandCruiser had struck Haines, leaving her badly injured. "It was crazy, I just ran out the front to see what was happening," he told reporters on Tuesday. He said he ran to assist the well-respected local MP, grabbing a knife from the alleged attacker's pocket and pulling him out of the car.

"He did have a knife. He didn't pull it out. I just wasn't comfortable with his movements, and so I basically just took it out of his pocket and threw it away," he said. Jefferies said he then held the man down until police arrived. "I just leant over him and once he was on the ground and he was no longer a threat, I just stood with him and I told him that he can't leave," he said.

Members of the police stand guard at the crime scene of a vehicle attack on Australian lawmaker Helen Haines in Wangaratta, Australia on Oct 19, 2026 in this screen grab obtained from a video. (Photo: Australian Broadcasting Corporation via Reuters)

Haines, 65, was airlifted to hospital where she underwent surgery overnight. She remains in a critical condition.  Early investigations suggested the driver, identified as a 43-year-old man, performed a U-turn before hitting Haines as she was loading or unloading things from the trunk of her car, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said . Counterterrorism authorities are among the multiple agencies involved in the investigation. While police have given no motive for the alleged attack, the involvement of counterterrorism investigators has raised alarm that it could have been an act of political violence, which is rare in Australia. Jefferies, whose shop is next door to Haines' electorate office around three hours' drive northeast of Melbourne, described the former midwife as a "genuine, kind person". Albanese praised Jefferies' intervention, calling him a hero. "At this dark and terrible time, an element of light is the fact that a Good Samaritan, someone rushed to Helen's defence in Wangaratta, put themselves potentially at risk by doing so. And that person is a hero today," Albanese said in an interview with the Nine network's "Today" show.  Jefferies downplayed the praise. "I don't think I'm a hero. I think that I just was a person who had an opportunity to intervene in a safe-ish sort of way," he said.

item.title: Rubio to encourage India's Reliance to produce, refine more Venezuelan oil
item.description: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio plans to encourage India's Reliance Industries to refine more Venezuelan crude at its local refineries and potentially begin producing oil in the South American country, he told reporters in Mumbai on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Gram Slattery
item.content:encoded: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio plans to encourage India's Reliance Industries (RELI.NS) to refine more Venezuelan crude at its local refineries and potentially begin producing oil in the South American country, he told reporters in Mumbai on Tuesday. Rubio landed in India's sweltering financial capital days after President Donald Trump waived potential sanctions on the world's top buyers of Russian oil, a list that includes India. The move is likely to help pave the way for a trade deal between New Delhi and Washington, but has been panned by US lawmakers, who complain that the Trump administration has been far too soft on Moscow. During the two-day visit to Mumbai and Jamnagar in the western part of the country, Rubio is slated to meet government and business leaders, including Foreign Minister S. Jaishankar and billionaire Mukesh Ambani, chairman of Reliance Industries, which operates the world's largest refining complex. "We will talk about (refining more Venezuelan crude) tomorrow with Reliance...They have done so in the past, and I think as more and more of Venezuelan oil comes online, that is something they can do," Rubio told reporters. Reliance's two massive refineries at the Jamnagar complex, with a combined capacity of about 1.4 million barrels per day of crude oil, are able to process the ultra-heavy crudes coming out of Venezuela, some of which have a sludge-like consistency. As Venezuela's oil production has increased following the Trump administration's capture of former Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro in January, Reliance has emerged as a significant importer of the nation's crude. Asked whether he would discuss the possibility of Reliance itself producing oil with Venezuela, Rubio said the matter had been discussed in the past, and that the matter would come up again. While Reliance is a major refiner of Venezuelan crude, it is not active inside the South American country. "We are going to go see what the holdup is and what opportunities exist...this is a company that has had a presence in Venezuela in the past, and whose refining capabilities are substantial," he said. NEW DELHI, WASHINGTON CLOSE IN ON TRADE DEAL Rubio's visit comes as Trump removed one potential stumbling block to a trade deal between the countries last Friday when he waived potential tariffs that would have punished New Delhi for its extensive purchases of Russian crude oil. Legislation signed by Trump in September authorizes the administration to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the top five importers of Russian oil, which would include India, which stands at number two on that list after China. Trump's decision to waive all substantive provisions of that bill has upset both Democrats and Republicans who have pushed him to up economic pressure on Moscow for its war with Ukraine. Rubio has said the effort to finalize a trade deal was a factor in the decision to waive those tariffs, and a comprehensive trade deal is almost complete, raising the possibility that it could be signed during his visit. He said the Trump administration was entering a 60-day review period, during which it would consider which new tariffs, if any, to impose. While the Trump administration has in the past pressed India to cut Russian oil imports, the US signed a deal with Russia last week to import diesel in a bid to cut domestic fuel prices before the midterm elections, making it unclear to what extent that remains a foreign policy priority. "Every country has a complex set of factors that they have to take into account," Rubio told reporters on Monday when asked about India's Russian oil purchases. India imports more than 85% of its crude oil requirements to help power its fast-growing economy. Rubio's India visit follows a trip to the Uzbekistan city of Samarkand, where he met Central Asian political and business leaders.

item.title: 午前のドル158円半ば、レンジ上限で動けず 円の弱さ指摘も
item.description:
Atsuko Aoyama
[東京 ２０日 ロイター] - 午前のドルは１５８円半ばでの膠着が続いた。直近のレンジ上限...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
午前のドル158円半ば、レンジ上限で動けず　円の弱さ指摘も 10/20 12:28 配信

米ドル紙幣。26年3月撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

Atsuko Aoyama

[東京 ２０日 ロイター] - 午前のドルは１５８円半ばでの膠着が続いた。直近のレンジ上限に当たり、上抜けるにも押し下げるにも材料に乏しいとの声がある。上値では日米の協調為替介入への警戒でドル買い／円売りに追随する動きは強まっていないが、他資産に比べた円の弱さが改めて意識されているとの見方も聞かれた。

・ドル／円、午前中は１５８円半ばで膠着

・直近のレンジの上限、２００日移動平均線近辺で上値重い

・来週以降のイベント待ちで動けずとの声も

・前日のドル／円はレンジ上抜け試す動き、円の弱さ浮き彫りとの声

・一部に高市早苗首相の財源巡るⅩ投稿を円売り材料視する向きも

・ドル１５９円台では円安けん制など口先介入に警戒

＜トレイダーズ証券の井口喜雄・市場部長＞

「ドル／円は直近のレンジ上限で２００日移動平均線近辺にあるが、ブレイクするようなイベントがない。じりじりとして動きが少なく、例えばレンジ上限で売るという判断も躊躇するところ」

「米国のＩＴ株が振るわない中でドルを買う理由にも乏しい。一方、市場が深刻なリスクオフとなった場合は円キャリーが剥がれてドル安／円高が進むかもれないが、今のような株の調整程度なら動意づくこともない」

「円買い理由があるとすれば日銀の利上げ加速だが、それが見えない。来年３－４月までの米国の利上げ観測を踏まえると金利差は一向に縮まらず、ドル／円を下目線ではみられない」

item.title: Gold steady as investors await fed rate signals
item.description: Gold prices were largely steady in a volatile session on Tuesday as investors awaited next week's Federal Reserve meeting for further direction on US interest rates.
item.dc:creator: Anushree Mukherjee
item.content:encoded: Gold prices were largely steady in a volatile session on Tuesday as investors awaited next week's Federal Reserve meeting for further direction on US interest rates. Spot gold was unchanged at $4,138.54 per ounce by 11:19 am EDT (1519 GMT). US gold futures for December delivery dropped 0.1% to $4,157.90 per ounce. "Inflation and the Fed's interest rates are the big stories that gold's fighting at the moment. US Treasuries do appear more favorable than gold as a safety asset for the moment," said Bob Haberkorn, senior market strategist at StoneX. "$4,000 is a big level for (gold) to keep an eye on and see if it can hold. A lot of that, at the moment, is going to be dependent on what the Fed says," Haberkorn said. The Fed raised interest rates by a quarter point in September, its first hike this year. While recent comments from [USN:L6N462084 TEXT:"Fed"] officials signaling little [USN:L1N4600EO TEXT:"urgency"] for further policy tightening have tempered expectations of a rate hike at the central bank's October 27-28 policy meeting, traders see a 92% chance of a hike in December, according to CME's FedWatch Tool . FEDWATCH Gold is still down around 26.4% from its record high of $5,594.82 in January and roughly 22% from levels at the start of the Iran war , when concerns over energy inflation reinforced bets on interest rate hikes. Gold is traditionally seen as an inflation hedge, but it loses its appeal as a non-yielding asset in a high-interest-rate environment. Investors are also watching next week's US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) data, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, for clues on whether inflation pressures remain persistent and how that could shape the rate outlook. In Japan, central bank Governor Kazuo Ueda [USN:L1N465004 TEXT:"said"] underlying inflation was "quite close" to the 2% target, signaling scope for further rate hikes. Among other metals, spot silver rose 1.5% to $57.92 per ounce, platinum gained 0.7% to $1,651.36 per ounce and palladium dropped 0.2% to $1,117.75 per ounce.

item.title: Dollar dips on AI worries, euro edges up despite French unrest
item.description: The US dollar slipped on Tuesday as doubts over the AI trade resurfaced, while the euro edged up despite traders' lingering worries about unrest in France.
item.dc:creator: Karen Brettell
item.content:encoded: The US dollar slipped on Tuesday as doubts over the AI trade resurfaced, while the euro edged up despite traders' lingering worries about unrest in France. Shares in South Korean AI services firm Elice Group (0158S0.KQ) plunged 32% in their Seoul [USN:L1N46600F TEXT:"market debut"], a sign that negative sentiment toward the AI sector in global markets is not easing. Strong capital inflows into US stocks have supported the dollar. Higher interest rates, driven partly by growth and inflation expectations tied to the sector, have also helped. "The dollar has been supported by big inflows into the equity market," said Dominic Bunning, head of G10 FX strategy at Nomura. Now, he said, "there is a lot more skepticism about the degree to which a lot of these companies will be profitable enough to justify the amount of issuance that having to be made at the moment … and whether this whole ecosystem can be profitable enough in the context of higher rates over a period of time." The dollar index , which measures the greenback against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro, fell 0.27% to 101.69, with the euro up 0.2% at $1.1232. Traders remained wary of the euro despite Tuesday's modest gains as France faces widespread protests and a worsening fiscal picture. The government said overnight curfews in violence-hit areas of France's biggest cities had brought [USN:L6N4660DJ TEXT:"some respite"] from the country's worst unrest in years. More protests are planned for the weekend. "The worries in France are not going away anytime soon," said Tommy von Brömsen, FX strategist at Handelsbanken. "The bearish view on France will stay for a while longer, and there's much more euro weakness to be priced in." Britain's pound strengthened 0.66% to $1.339 after labour market data showed a resilient [USN:L8N46608R TEXT:"jobs market"], the latest batch of data from the UK that surprised to the upside. "The risk is that a resilient labour market gives the Bank of England both the room and the reason to raise interest rates again," said Lale Akoner, global market strategist at eToro. "Sterling could benefit from rising rate expectations." Markets are almost fully pricing in a 25-basis-point rate hike by the Bank of England at its next meeting on November 5, according to LSEG data. STRONG JAPANESE BOND AUCTION The yen jumped after an auction of longer-dated Japanese government bonds (JGBs) drew [USN:L1N46604J TEXT:"record demand"]. "The record 20-year auction is a strong signal that sidelined cash is finally coming back," said Masahiko Loo, senior fixed-income strategist at State Street Investment Management in Tokyo. "JGBs are also starting to look like a relative haven from Europe's political and fiscal volatility, particularly around France.” The Japanese yen gained 0.29% against the greenback to 158.04 per dollar. Elsewhere, the Canadian dollar rose 0.42% to 1.405 per US dollar, its strongest level in almost a month, after Alberta residents voted by a [USN:L6N4651AT TEXT:"large majority"] to remain part of Canada in the province's first-ever referendum on separation.

item.title: Brent slips in choppy session as investors weigh attacks on ships, Saudi energy
item.description: Oil prices slipped from a five-month high during a choppy session on Tuesday as traders priced in Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf.
item.dc:creator: Georgina Mccartney
item.content:encoded: Oil prices slipped from a five-month high during a choppy session on Tuesday as traders priced in Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and reports of vessel attacks in the Gulf. Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Monday they launched [USN:S8N44M08Y TEXT:"several attacks"] on Saudi energy, airport and military targets, such as an Aramco (2222.SE) site in Yanbu, the Shaybah oilfield, Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport and Abha airport. Saudi authorities did not immediately confirm the Houthi claims and Reuters could not independently verify them. Brent crude futures fell 67 cents or 0.61% to $108.88 at 10:09 a.m. EDT. Earlier in the session the front-month contract reached $111.99, a five-month high. The November contract for US West Texas Intermediate crude, which expires on Tuesday, was up 88 cents or 0.85% at $104.54, down from the session high of 110.48, the highest since April for a nearby contract. The more active December contract was down 45 cents or 0.46% at $98.09 a barrel. "Oil prices remain well-supported ... This suggests the market is pricing in a significant risk premium, given the situation's volatility," ING analysts said in a note on Tuesday. At least 18 vessels were reportedly attacked over two weeks, which keeps the risk premium intact, shiptracker Kpler said in a note on Monday. Also on Monday, a Houthi [USN:L1N46509O TEXT:"attack"] on a training camp for government security forces in Yemen's Shabwa province killed 58 people and injured more than 200. The renewed attacks heightened fears about regional stability and underscored continuing risks to energy supply from the region, keeping oil prices above $100 a barrel. DIESEL SUPPLY CRUNCH Russian diesel cargoes are returning to their traditional destinations after the [USN:L6N4660Q8 TEXT:"US suspended sanctions"] and secured the lifting of an export ban, with at least two tankers signaling trips to Turkey and Brazil in recent days, according to shipping data from Kpler and LSEG. The US is [USN:L1N4660KS TEXT:"working with domestic refiners"] to squeeze more crude through the refining complex, US Energy Department Under Secretary Kyle Haustveit said on Tuesday at the Drake Forum in Titusville, Pennsylvania. In the US, analysts expected crude oil stockpiles to have fallen last week along with product inventories, a preliminary Reuters [USN:L4N4651EI TEXT:"poll"] showed on Monday.

item.title: Trump open to idea of joint meeting with Xi, Putin next month
item.description: Nuclear talks between the US, China and Russia could happen as soon as next month after Donald Trump says he is open to a three-way summit.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

Trump open to idea of joint meeting with Xi, Putin next month

Nuclear talks between the US, China and Russia could happen as soon as next month after Donald Trump says he is open to a three-way summit.

Traditional Russian wooden dolls depicting China's President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin are displayed for sale at a souvenir shop in St Petersburg, Russia on Nov 21, 2024. (File photo: AP/Dmitri Lovetsky)

FAST

WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said on Monday (Oct 19) he is open to three-way arms-control talks with the leaders of China and Russia as soon as next month, raising the prospect of an unprecedented meeting and a major diplomatic gambit for the US president. "We would have it to talk about nuclear weapons and denuclearisation," Trump told reporters outside the White House. "If President Xi wants to have it, I'd have it. I'm sure we'd talk about other things like trade too." Trump has tried to thaw frosty relations with Beijing and Moscow as those non-Western powers grow closer. A three-way meeting would also raise alarm from Europe to Asia over private deals that weaken Washington's transatlantic and Indo-Pacific alliances. But a deal struck between the three countries could also lower global tensions. An end to Russia's war in Ukraine could resolve the biggest threat in decades to European security, and a deal on arms would bind the three nations with the biggest stockpiles of nuclear weapons.

In recent days, Trump has moved to warm ties with Russian President Vladimir Putin, announcing a diesel-fuel deal and signing an order on Friday waiving key sanctions on Moscow . Trump has also sought stable relations with Chinese President Xi Jinping, who in turn has nurtured close ties with Putin. So far, Trump has not delivered on a campaign promise to quickly end the war in Ukraine. The White House has been discussing for weeks a possible meeting between the leaders focused on denuclearisation on the sidelines of the Nov 18-19 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China, according to a person familiar with the matter. Putin later pitched using such a meeting to negotiate an end to the four-year-old Ukraine conflict in a manner that would favour Moscow, the Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the discussions. Putin's suggestion came during an Oct 9 phone call with Trump that yielded the deal on Russian diesel. Earlier on Monday, the Kremlin said that the potential meeting had come up in talks. The three leaders have met separately but never held formal talks together. The White House did not respond to a Reuters request for comment. The Russian and Chinese embassies in Washington also did not reply to requests for comment. Trump's diesel deal with Putin and the executive order waiving sanctions on Moscow have drawn criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy , who has warned they would embolden Putin and prolong the war. Speaking about the possible meeting on Monday, Trump said, "I would do it, not so much for Ukraine because Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine." He added that "Zelenskiy is not helping matters much," and that "it's time for somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine." Moscow launched one of its broadest air assaults in months overnight, cutting power to more than half a million households and damaging energy infrastructure across Ukraine. Ten people were reported killed.

Related:

Commentary: Why do Trump and Xi keep meeting if the hard issues remain unresolved?

US and China discuss reciprocal visits to nuclear sites: Reports

TRUMP SEEKS NUCLEAR TALKS Last week, Trump told reporters he thought a denuclearisation deal with Russia and China was possible, but that it "doesn't have to be this year." It's not clear how advanced any talks between the countries are. Russia has the most stored nuclear warheads, followed by the United States and China, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. The Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty expired earlier this year. The New START treaty, signed in 2010, allowed a single extension, which Putin and former US President Joe Biden agreed to for five years. Any new extension would require an executive decision to voluntarily extend the limits of the treaty. China's foreign ministry said last week that its "nuclear strength is by no means at the same level with that of the US and Russia" and that it would be "neither fair, reasonable nor realistic to ask China to join the so-called trilateral nuclear disarmament negotiations at this stage." Trump has already agreed to attend the APEC summit in Shenzhen next month, marking his second trip to China this year and his third visit with Xi over the same period. China, Russia and the United States are all members of APEC. On Monday, Trump downplayed the idea of another high-profile meeting in China, with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. "I get along with him very well, and I'm not sure that anybody's asking for a meeting," he said. Trump previously said he planned to meet with Kim this year. North Korea has publicly indicated that it is not open to talks aimed at convincing Pyongyang to give up its nuclear weapons.

item.title: South Korean firm's debut plunge adds to investor concerns about AI spending
item.description: A 32% drop in shares of South Korea's Elice Group on Tuesday renewed investor concerns about the sustainability and the payoff cycle for the vast amount of capital pouring into the AI buildout amid growing scrutiny of company valuations.
item.dc:creator: Heejin Kim, Yantoultra Ngui
item.content:encoded: A 32% drop in shares of South Korea's Elice Group (0158S0.KQ) on Tuesday renewed investor concerns about the sustainability and the payoff cycle for the vast amount of capital pouring into the AI buildout amid growing scrutiny of company valuations. The plunge in shares of the provider of AI cloud services as well as AI-based education and business software made it the worst debut ever in South Korea for a company that raised more than $100 million in an IPO, according to Dealogic data. Elice raised 201.1 billion won ($150 million) in its IPO, and said that it planned to spend most of the proceeds on launching portable modular data centres and related infrastructure. The stock's poor first day of trading contributed to [USN:L6N4660RT TEXT:"renewed weakness"] in AI-linked stocks on Wall Street on Tuesday, with shares in neocloud firms including CoreWeave (CRWV.O) and Nebius Group (NBIS.O) both falling more than 5%. Elice's slide had earlier weighed on the broader South Korean market, a poster child for global AI trade and investor sentiment, with the benchmark KOSPI (.KS11) falling 3.73% to its lowest closing level since April 7. After dominating market gains, AI companies are now facing more sceptical investors as concerns over spending, competition and profitability eclipse optimism about AI's long-term potential. Elevated inflation has also pushed interest rates higher, meaning the AI sector's debt will become more expensive to repay. S&P Global estimates the world's biggest tech firms are likely to have more [USN:L8N4651G6 TEXT:"AI-linked liabilities"] than currently known. Elice's IPO was priced on October 6, before the recent selloff in AI-related stocks. "The conclusion is simple: the timing is bad. The latest chip selloff has bruised investors' appetite, and the poor debut is certainly a warning for upcoming AI listings," said Swissquote analyst Ipek Ozkardeskaya. "The good news is that AI headlines could change from one minute to the next. One great development and the rally could be back," she said, adding the sector's upside potential continues to compete with the downside risks from high valuations. INCREASING SCRUTINY OF AI INFRA DEALS Elice's shares closed at 60,500 won compared with its IPO pricing of 90,500 won, leaving it valued at roughly 674 billion won ($508 million). The IPO drew institutional orders worth 388.84 times the shares available in the offering. Its poor debut came after other AI companies dropped or suspended deals in recent days, as investors reassess whether the firms racing to build the infrastructure underpinning AI can generate returns that justify [USN:L4N45Z0RI TEXT:"soaring spending"]. The IPO of Australia's [USN:L1N45U12T TEXT:"Firmus"], which is backed by Nvidia (NVDA.O) , was shelved, while Blackstone-backed (BX.N) [USN:L4N45Z0H4 TEXT:"AirTrunk"] postponed a Singapore listing, and [USN:L6N45H0SG TEXT:"SB Energy"], a unit of SoftBank (9984.T) , delayed its US share sale. Investors are increasingly scrutinising AI infrastructure and data centre deals, said Ke Yan, head of research at Singapore-based Shenton Research, and were now focused on those firms' customer contracts and committed revenue figures. "Everyone is not sure how much demand for AI there will be and it is hard to estimate current demand," said Kim Hak-joon, an analyst at Seoul-based Kiwoom Securities. Elice's revenue for the first half of the year tripled to 34 billion won and it swung to an operating profit of 10 billion won compared with a 3.5 billion won loss for the same period a year earlier. The company's largest shareholder is chief executive and co-founder Kim Jae Won, who holds 34.6%, ahead of Silicon Valley investor Altos with 24.45% and the Korea Development Bank, which owns 6.45%, according to company filings. ($1 = 1,327.2800 won)

item.title: Hegseth discusses Iran with Netanyahu in unannounced visit to Israel, officials say
item.description: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth discussed Iran with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during an unannounced visit to Israel on Monday, three Israeli officials said, as tensions flare between the US and Iran.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth discussed Iran with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during an unannounced visit to Israel on Monday, three Israeli officials said, as tensions flare between the US and Iran . Doron Spielman, a spokesperson for the prime minister, later confirmed to Reuters that Netanyahu had met with Hegseth at the Uvda air force base in Israel's southern Negev desert region. Netanyahu and Hegseth discussed "the threats in the region" and the US-Israel partnership in dealing both offensively and defensively with those threats, he said in a brief phone call. Hegseth also thanked Israel for hosting US forces, which Spielman said numbered in the thousands, and discussed President Donald Trump's support for the prime minister. "There's a deep personal relationship here that was at the core of this discussion," Spielman said. On Sunday, Trump [USN:L1N46403J TEXT:"endorsed"] Netanyahu in next week's parliamentary election in Israel, the country's first ballot since the October 7, 2023, Hamas attack on southern Israel. The Pentagon has not publicly commented on Hegseth's visit. Hegseth earlier posted on X that he had visited US service members in the Central Command area of responsibility, which covers the Middle East, northeast Africa and parts of Asia. He did not specify where he had met with the forces. Hegseth's visit comes as tensions flare between the US and Iran over the [USN:S8N43Z00H TEXT:"Strait of Hormuz"] and as Yemen's Iran-allied [USN:S8N43T03Z TEXT:"Houthis intensify their attacks"] on Saudi Arabia. US and Israeli forces launched joint strikes against Iran in late February, setting off the wider Middle East war. Netanyahu told Israeli media this month that he's [USN:L1N4600GP TEXT:"not seeking to attack Iran"] before the October 27 Israeli election. Trump has said he will [USN:FWN45U1SW TEXT:"not attack Iran"] before US midterm elections in November. Israel has hosted additional US forces, including military aircraft, since at least February as part of the war with Iran.

item.title: France in turmoil: What might follow a weekend of riots?
item.description: France is counting the cost of some of its worst unrest in years at the weekend over the cost of living and under-funded public services. Here is the latest:
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: France is counting the cost of some of its [USN:L1N46401W TEXT:"worst unrest in years"] at the weekend over the cost of living and under-funded public services. Here is the latest: HOW WILL THE GOVERNMENT STOP MORE VIOLENCE AND HELP VICTIMS? Authorities say 2,500 people are in custody awaiting questioning while 149 are detained awaiting trial. [USN:L8N4650PE TEXT:"Partial curfews"] have been imposed in parts of Paris, Bordeaux, Lille, Lyon, Nice and Marseille to keep the streets quiet in areas worst-hit by rioting. The government, which had 60,000 officers mobilised at the weekend, plans to increase police numbers on the ground. For businesses and victims of violence, the government is implementing state-financed furlough measures to avoid layoffs, and providing funds to help companies meet cashflow needs. Insurers have promised speedy payouts to cover some of the damage, which hit more than 3,000 shops. HOW WILL THE GOVERNMENT ADDRESS UNDERLYING COMPLAINTS? France's extremely strained public finances mean the government has precious little room for broader measures to address protesters' anger over the rising cost of living. It has already hiked emergency spending this year to help certain sectors like farmers, fishermen and haulers cope with high fuel costs caused by the Iran war . The protests [USN:L1N45S0C7 TEXT:"began last month at high schools"] in Paris' working-class northern suburbs, where anger over teacher shortages and shabby facilities evolved into a broader movement. The government has so far not committed to substantial extra funding for schools but [USN:L6N45V0FM TEXT:"has pledged"] to send some 3,000 teachers, who are qualified but not yet working, to fill staffing gaps. HAVE PROTESTS PEAKED? Cities [USN:L6N4660DJ TEXT:"were quieter"] at the start of the week. But some protesters have called for a new round of demonstrations on Saturday. Unions have called for strikes on November 5 to protest budget cuts and support hiking wages. Schools are on a break for two weeks, but some student organisations are calling for more demonstrations. HOW WILL FRANCE'S DIRE ECONOMIC SITUATION BE AFFECTED? The unrest is a blow to business confidence, which was already fragile due to a fiscal crisis and high energy prices. The minority government is struggling to pass spending cuts in a divided parliament as part of its 2027 budget and is at risk of being toppled by opposition parties if a compromise cannot be found with at least some of them. The government wants to cut its budget deficit to 5.0% of economic output next year from 5.4% this year – one of the biggest in the euro zone. French bond yields [USN:L6N4660NP TEXT:"climbed further"] on Tuesday after their biggest daily rise in nearly a month in the previous session, with investors remaining cautious. The yield on France's 10-year benchmark bond reached 4.96% at one point on Tuesday. WILL THE UNREST SPREAD TO OTHER COUNTRIES? If France cannot contain the unrest, there is a risk that it could [USN:L8N4611KF TEXT:"spill across its borders"] with deep public anger around Europe over cost-of-living issues. In neighbouring Italy, [USN:L8N46407Z TEXT:"clashes erupted"] between police and protesters on Sunday. Albania has also seen a series of student demonstrations in recent days over corruption, a lack of jobs and poor education standards, while Spain and Portugal have faced protests over housing. HOW WILL THE UNREST AFFECT THE 2027 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTION? Elections next year will see President Emmanuel Macron step down after a decade in power. The unrest is likely to boost far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen, who is already the frontrunner in polls and has long talked tough on law and order. "Le Pen no longer needs to spend any money to campaign," Jean-Baptiste Moreau, a former lawmaker from Macron's camp, [USN:L6N4650JF TEXT:"told Reuters"]. "It's not just a clear path ahead of her, it's a six-lane highway." Hard-left candidate Jean-Luc Melenchon has come under pressure for backing protesters' demands, criticising the government's handling and not clearly condemning the violence. Meanwhile, Macron, who headed off to the Middle East on Monday, has emerged from the crisis further weakened. His former Prime Minister Edouard Philippe, now a centre-right presidential candidate, said on X he wanted "decisions and initiatives" from the lame-duck leader to "restore order". ARE PARIS AND OTHER CITIES SAFE TO VISIT? There have been no reports of any injuries to foreigners caught up in the unrest. However, several European governments [USN:L8N4650JR TEXT:"advised citizens"] travelling to France to avoid large crowds and exercise caution.

item.title: France's unrest lays bare 'slow agony' of Macron's twilight months
item.description: The civil unrest has exposed the powerlessness of a leader struggling to contain social anger.
item.dc:creator: Michel Rose
item.content:encoded: France’s worst bout of civil unrest in years has plunged President Emmanuel Macron’s final months in office deeper into [USN:FWN4630KA TEXT:"turmoil"], exposing the powerlessness of a leader struggling to contain social anger with little money to spend, scant political capital and an increasingly fragile grip on public order. The [USN:L1N46302B TEXT:"rioting"] that swept across France on Saturday, leaving a trail of looted shops, torched buildings and defaced public institutions, presents Macron with perhaps the most explosive challenge of his twilight presidency: a country demanding more from a state that can no longer afford to give much. Macron came to power almost a decade ago promising to upend France’s sclerotic political class, turbocharge economic reforms and restore authority through a more assertive presidency. Instead, with just six months left in office, he finds himself effectively a lame-duck head of state presiding over a country mired in political paralysis, facing acute [USN:L6N46502R TEXT:"financial pressures"] and grappling with unrest that has exposed the limits of state authority. Unlike during the Yellow Vest uprising of 2018-2019, when Macron sought to defuse public anger with billions of euros in concessions, France’s strained public finances and fractured parliament leave him with precious few levers to pull. Even former allies are now openly scathing, tracing the country's current impasse to Macron's decision to call a [USN:L8N3J00J1 TEXT:"snap parliamentary election"] in 2024 that weakened his authority. “The end of this term is a slow agony,” said Loïc Kervran, a former lawmaker from Macron’s camp, on X. “The president paralysed the country with his absurd decision to dissolve parliament in 2024. Arguably the worst decision in the history of the Fifth Republic." LE PEN'S 'HIGHWAY' TO THE PRESIDENCY The turmoil may benefit far-right National Rally leader Marine Le Pen, who is already the frontrunner in the 2027 presidential race and stands to gain from both the anger over declining living standards and the fears over law and order unleashed by the weekend’s violence. "Le Pen no longer needs to spend any money to campaign," Jean-Baptiste Moreau, another former Macron lawmaker, told Reuters. "It's not just a clear path ahead of her — it's a six-lane highway." Le Pen delivered her own message to the nation in a video statement on Sunday, portraying Macron's administration as a crumbling power and casting herself as the figure capable of restoring order. When Macron later addressed the country, he offered little concrete action, stopping short of declaring a state of emergency. As he spoke, looting was continuing for a second consecutive night, including in affluent Paris districts, prompting his prime minister Sébastien Lecornu to announce local curfews on Monday. Opponents and one-time allies alike were underwhelmed. His former prime minister, Edouard Philippe, now preparing his own presidential run, was unsparing in his criticism. "Mr President, I listened to you last night," he wrote on X. "I would have preferred, like millions of French people, decisions and initiatives to restore order." "Our country needs to be commanded," he added. But even Philippe is struggling to shake off his past association with Macron, and most recent polls show far-left firebrand Jean-Luc Melenchon edging ahead of him in the race to qualify for the second-round runoff vote. That outcome would all but guarantee a Le Pen victory, according to opinion polls. CALLS FOR EARLY RESIGNATION AMID MULTIPLE CRISES Macron's office on Monday announced that he had refused his interior minister's resignation and ordered a review into apparent failures in intelligence gathering and police preparedness — deepening the impression of a government struggling to regain control. [USN:L1N465097 TEXT:"Investors also took fright"]. Market analysts say the violence adds another layer of political risk at a time when France is already under scrutiny over its swelling debt burden and struggle to reduce one of the euro zone's largest budget deficits. The president now finds himself trapped between bond markets demanding spending restraint and protesters demanding the opposite. Despite calls from opponents to remain in France, Macron arrived in Kuwait on Monday on a Gulf tour he says will help secure fuel supplies and ease some of the economic pressures that have helped swell the ranks of the protesters. The trip carries risks, reinforcing perceptions of a president disconnected from the public mood. Images of Macron attending a Céline Dion concert with his wife Brigitte on Friday evening, hours before the unrest erupted, prompted ridicule on social media and became an easy symbol for critics seeking to portray him as detached from events. In a sign of the depth of disenchantment in parts of his political camp, some former allies have begun openly discussing whether he should leave office before the end of his term. Moreau, who spoke to Macron on Sunday, said he urged him to prepare an orderly early departure to break the current political deadlock and avoid another six months of drift. "He doesn't want to give up, that's not his character. But that's what he should do for the country," he said.

item.title: Governments warn citizens over security in France after riots
item.description: Governments in Europe and Asia, including China, on Monday advised citizens travelling to France to avoid large crowds and exercise caution, warning of a deterioration in security conditions after thousands were arrested and shops looted in protests over the weekend.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Governments in Europe and Asia, including China, on Monday advised citizens travelling to France to avoid large crowds and exercise caution, warning of a [USN:L6N4650BY TEXT:"deterioration in security conditions"] after thousands were arrested and shops looted in protests over the weekend. Demonstrations across France over high prices and declining public services [USN:L1N46401W TEXT:"erupted into riots"] on Saturday, with a town hall torched as violent groups clashed with police. In response, the foreign ministries of several European countries issued fresh travel warnings. ITALY Italy said its citizens should register their presence in France on a website or an app to enable them to be located, as it warned them to avoid large crowds and exercise extreme caution. GERMANY The German foreign ministry said further riots in the coming days couldn't be ruled out and urged German nationals to follow instructions from local police. It warned citizens that they could face fines or claims for damages if they failed to leave unauthorised demonstrations when asked to do so. CZECH REPUBLIC Czechs in France are advised to avoid demonstrations, marches and public gatherings, CTK news agency reported. The security situation in France has deteriorated, according to the Czech foreign affairs ministry. POLAND Poland said in its country guidance that visitors should avoid places where demonstrations are taking place, though there was no change to its overall guidance about whether France was safe to visit. NETHERLANDS The Dutch government in an advisory last updated on October 7 warned travelers to France to avoid protests. NORDICS Denmark, Sweden, Finland and Norway have issued advisories urging their citizens in France to avoid demonstrations and follow the guidance of local authorities. CHINA China's Foreign Ministry and diplomatic missions in France have urged Chinese nationals planning to travel to the country to remain alert to potential risks, strengthen safety precautions, and avoid areas where demonstrations are taking place, according to state media. MALAYSIA Malaysia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs said it is monitoring the demonstrations and that while travel to France remains unrestricted, Malaysians are advised to consider postponing non-essential trips until the situation improves. It said its embassy in Paris has issued an advisory urging Malaysians in France to exercise caution and remain vigilant.

item.title: Polish satellite maker Creotech plans tenfold capacity boost, warns of Europe’s US rocket reliance
item.description: Polish satellite maker Creotech Instruments plans to raise its production capacity by up to tenfold by 2029, CEO Grzegorz Brona said on Friday, while warning Europe would remain reliant on US rockets to put its satellites into orbit for years.
item.dc:creator: Stefan Gardawski, Marta Maciag
item.content:encoded: Polish satellite maker Creotech Instruments (CRI1.WA) plans to raise its production capacity by up to tenfold by 2029, CEO Grzegorz Brona said on Friday, while warning Europe would remain reliant on US rockets to put its satellites into orbit for years. Brona spoke with Reuters in Sopot two days after Ukraine said SpaceX (SPCX.O) had [USN:L8N4600M6 TEXT:"curbed its use of Starshield"], the military-grade version of the Starlink satellite network. Shares of Eutelsat (ETL.PA) , widely seen as Europe's leading challenger to Starlink, [USN:L8N4620IW TEXT:"jumped 23%"] on Wednesday and closed the week 28% higher. Asked whether European industry could build an alternative to Starlink, Brona said the continent could produce thousands of satellites and still have no one to launch them. "Launch vehicles are now becoming a means of political pressure on the European Union in the hands of (US President) Donald Trump's administration," he said. Europe carried out 8 of the world's 324 orbital launches last year, against 193 by the US. Starlink alone accounted for more than 60% of active satellites, according to European Space Agency data. Creotech, which does not build rockets, has kept US technology out of its satellites to avoid US arms export rules, under which Washington can block sales of a satellite containing even a small American part. Yet it still relies on US rockets. SpaceX carried all four satellites Creotech built for Poland's MikroGlob military programme into orbit. "Of course, Europe is waking up," Brona said, pointing to new European rocket programmes including a [USN:L1N44Y01P TEXT:"German launcher"], but added that building enough rockets would probably take a decade. Separately, he said [USN:L8N3YS0MG TEXT:"programmes"] for several large EU satellite constellations — fleets of spacecraft working as one system — were already under way, and that Creotech aimed to bid in their tenders. The satellite maker plans to open a factory in 2029 able to make 40 satellites a year of mixed types, or up to 100 of one model, compared with about 10 at its current plant. Brona added Creotech would start opening subsidiaries in France and Germany in the coming weeks and was aiming to build 500-kg satellites by 2032. Revenue for next year is secured, and the company will probably sign several more contracts within six months, Brona said.

item.title: Antofagasta’s Centinela strike ends after deal with unions
item.description: Workers from two unions at Chile’s Centinela copper mine have ratified an agreement reached with Antofagasta Minerals on a new collective bargaining contra
item.dc:creator: Mining.com
item.content:encoded: Workers from two unions at Chile’s Centinela copper mine have ratified an agreement reached with Antofagasta Minerals on a new collective bargaining contract, ending a strike of more than a week, the unions and the company said on Sunday. More than 700 members of the Distrito Centinela and Minera Esperanza unions began the strike on October 7 after contract talks broke down. They had sought equal benefits for workers regardless of which union they belonged to. The parties returned to the negotiating table on Tuesday in an effort to resolve the dispute. “The Distrito Centinela and Minera Esperanza unions announce the successful conclusion of our collective bargaining process, after 94.49% of participating workers voted to approve the proposed collective agreement,” the unions said in a statement, which was followed by a company statement confirming the deal. Three workers had been on a hunger strike in an effort to pressure both sides into finding a solution to the deadlocked talks. Antofagasta said on Wednesday it had managed to maintain production at normal levels, avoiding any negative impact from the strike at the mine, which produced 240,400 metric tons of copper in 2025. The strike at Centinela, along with the ultimately unrealized risk of a supervisors’ strike at BHP’s Escondida mine, had been supporting global copper prices amid concerns about the industry’s ability to increase supply sufficiently to meet expected future demand. (Reporting by Fabian Cambero; Editing by William Mallard)

item.title: US Project Vault readies $1B loan blitz for industry
item.description: Federal-backed financing aims to help US manufacturers secure essential metals and materials amid supply risks.
item.dc:creator: Cecilia Jamasmie
item.content:encoded:
US Project Vault readies $1B loan blitz for industry

Staff Writer | October 16, 2026 | 5:39 am Battery Metals   Critical Minerals   Suppliers & Equipment   Africa   USA   Cobalt   Copper   Lithium   Nickel   Rare Earth   Specialty Minerals

Trump addressing coal industry representatives. ( Image courtesy of The White House. )

The US government-backed Project Vault is preparing to issue up to $1 billion in loans to American manufacturers seeking critical minerals, advancing Washington’s efforts to shield domestic industry from supply disruptions.

VaultCo, the entity managing the stockpiling initiative, is in discussions with more than 70 companies across the critical minerals supply chain, Bloomberg reported . The first round of financing is expected to cover more than a dozen original equipment manufacturers (OEMs), with another group to follow.

“What’s likely to happen is we’ll announce several hundred million dollars, maybe a billion dollars, of loans to OEMs who have requested use of the Vault facility,” VaultCo Executive Chairman Brett Lambert told the news outlet. “In the first tranche, we’ll have more than a dozen firms, followed by more than a dozen shortly after.”

The financing would mark a significant step towards making Project Vault operational as the US seeks to reduce its exposure to volatile critical minerals markets and strengthen manufacturers’ access to materials essential for industrial production.

Trump launches $12B ‘Project Vault’ to cut China reliance

Lambert said the recipients would not be publicly identified at this stage, although the announcement is expected to disclose the types of minerals they have requested.

Stockpile takes shape

Launched in February , Project Vault is structured as an independently governed public-private partnership backed by a $10 billion loan from the US Export-Import Bank (EXIM) and nearly $2 billion in private investment.

Commodity trading giants Glencore (LON: GLEN) and Mercuria recently committed $500 million each , becoming the first commodity traders to join the initiative.

Mercuria has already delivered 12,000 tonnes of copper from the Democratic Republic of Congo , establishing a new destination for the African country’s metal within Washington’s supply security strategy.

Glencore, Mercuria to help build US minerals stockpile with $1B EXIM financing

The shipment comes amid growing US demand for Congolese copper. Imports reached a record 53,290 tonnes in July, driven by competitive prices, improved product quality and concerns over potential tariffs that prompted buyers to accelerate shipments.

Commercial imports and Project Vault serve different purposes. While conventional purchases meet immediate industrial demand, the reserve is intended to provide manufacturers with access to materials when normal supply channels become disrupted.

Tailored mineral demand

Unlike conventional government stockpiles, Project Vault is designed around manufacturers’ specific requirements rather than predetermined inventories of strategic commodities.

Participating companies have requested not only raw metals and minerals but also specialized magnets, powders, alloys and other processed materials tailored to their production needs.

“There isn’t any one mineral that stands out, but the specificity of the requests have surprised me,” Lambert told Bloomberg .

The demand-driven approach allows manufacturers to determine which materials are purchased and stored, potentially giving smaller buyers greater purchasing power in fragmented and often opaque markets.

Op-Ed: US has built a strategic copper reserve. Now can it keep it?

It also distinguishes Project Vault from the US National Defense Stockpile , which the Defense Logistics Agency administers to secure materials required for national defence.

The next test will be whether the initial loans can translate manufacturers’ highly specific requests into reliable inventories, particularly for processed materials that may be harder to source than raw commodities.

item.title: Tech giants come knocking for a piece of Anglo American as copper scarcity bites, Wanblad tells FT
item.description: Wanblad says "deep expressions of interest" from tech companies have yet to turn into a stake, while Beijing holds the key to the $54 billion Teck merger.
item.dc:creator: Frik Els
item.content:encoded:
Tech giants come knocking for a piece of Anglo American as copper scarcity bites, Wanblad tells FT

Frik Els | October 15, 2026 | 10:55 am Markets   Top Companies   Africa   Australia   Canada   China   Latin America   Copper   Diamond   Nickel   Palladium   Platinum

Los Bronces copper mine in Chile. ( Image courtesy of Anglo American | Flickr. )

Anglo American (LON: AAL) has held talks with technology companies interested in buying equity in the miner as a way of securing supplies of the metals that go into data centres, chief executive Duncan Wanblad told the Financial Times’ Metals and Mining Summit in London on Thursday.

Discussions were “absolutely being had”, Wanblad said, with the question from the tech side coming down to whether to lock in long-term offtake directly or take an equity position to secure a stake in future supply. No stakes have been taken, but there had been “deep expressions of interest” in doing so, he told the summit. “Given the scarcity issue that we’ve been speaking about, a lot of people are looking for ways to secure supply.”

Comex copper for December delivery traded near $6.52 a pound (about $14,370 a tonne) on Thursday, a third straight decline, after stronger than expected US inflation data put a Federal Reserve rate hike this month back on the table. Cash copper on the LME settled at a record $14,822 on Monday and the most-active Comex contract remains within 6% of its September 9 record settlement of $6.89.

A $90 billion copper company

Anglo’s New York-listed shares added 0.6% to $26.86 in early trade on Thursday for a market value of $58.0 billion, while Teck Resources (NYSE: TECK) edged up 0.3% to $64.96 and is worth $31.9 billion. At those prices Anglo-Teck would carry a combined nominal value of just under $90 billion, up from the $53 billion the two companies put on the merger of equals when it was announced in September last year .

Teck has been the better performer since, gaining 50% over the past 12 months against 36% for Anglo, and both are among the strongest diversified miners of 2026. The combination would rank alongside Glencore at $89 billion and Freeport-McMoRan at $99 billion.

Waiting on Beijing

The approaches come while Anglo waits on China for the final clearance on the merger with Teck, a combination that would rank among the five largest copper producers with annual output of about 1.2 million tonnes. Wanblad would not be drawn at the summit on what Chinese regulators want in return for approval, according to the FT.

China’s State Administration for Market Regulation has asked Anglo to commit to a steady flow of copper concentrate to Chinese smelters, including volumes sold through traders, as a condition for clearing the deal, Reuters reported on October 2. The remedies under discussion do not include asset sales. The combined group would control around 5% of global copper supply, well below the 10% to 15% thresholds that normally trigger competition concerns, but China refines up to 60% of the world’s copper cathode and is facing its worst feedstock shortage in decades. Canada , the EU , the US, Japan, Chile and South Korea have all signed off, and the parties still expect to close by March 2027.

Wanblad said in August that mining transactions now take “probably a little bit longer than they might have done five years ago”, with companies needing to allow 12 to 18 months for approvals , while rejecting the idea that regulation was making deals impossible to get done.

Nickel closure on the table

Anglo is also likely to shut its nickel business in Brazil if the European Union does not approve the planned $500 million sale of the assets to China’s MMG, Wanblad told the conference. The European Commission opened an in-depth probe of the deal late last year over fears MMG could divert ferronickel from Codemin and Barro Alto away from European stainless steel makers, and issued a formal warning last month. MMG has since proposed long-term European supply commitments .

Anglo’s Brazil chief operating officer Ruben Fernandes told a closed hearing in Brussels last week that MMG was the only credible buyer the company had identified and that a prohibition would leave it heading for care and maintenance as the pathway to closure.

The nickel sale and the Teck merger are the two remaining pieces of a portfolio simplification that also has Anglo seeking about $1 billion for De Beers .

item.title: Copper price forecasts lifted for 2026 but tariff “collapse” still on the table
item.description: Macquarie’s collapse scenario needs Washington to rule tariffs out, which it rates least likely. More likely is limbo past January 1, with 1.5 million tonnes of US copper staying exactly where it is.
item.dc:creator: Frik Els
item.content:encoded:
Copper price forecasts lifted for 2026 but tariff “collapse” still on the table

Staff Writer | October 14, 2026 | 9:31 am Critical Minerals   Markets   China   Latin America   USA   Copper

Where do we send these? Credit: Glencore

Copper pulled back from a three-week high on Wednesday after US inflation data put a Federal Reserve rate hike this month back on the table, and word of a preliminary deal to avert a strike at BHP’s Escondida, the world’s largest copper mine, took some of the supply premium out of the price.

Comex copper for December delivery traded at $6.6695 a pound (about $14,704 a tonne) late morning in New York, down 0.8%, after touching $6.7890 earlier in the session. The most-active contract’s record settlement of $6.89 was set on September 9 , the day before a report that the White House tariff plan had stalled knocked more than 5% off the price.

In London, three-month copper climbed as far as $14,700 a tonne, its highest since September 23, before easing to $14,532 by early afternoon. Cash copper settled at a record $14,822 on Monday and $14,741 on Tuesday, and LME inventories have fallen for seven straight sessions to 229,650 tonnes.

US consumer prices accelerated in September on a surge in gasoline costs, and the CME’s FedWatch tool put the odds of a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s late-October meeting at about 44%, double the day before, Reuters reported. New York Fed President John Williams said he still sees one more hike this year.

Two sources told Reuters that Escondida’s supervisors’ union and the company had reached a preliminary agreement , which members were voting on Wednesday morning, and a union leader told Bloomberg a deal was “virtually done”. Unions at Antofagasta’s Centinela returned to talks on Tuesday after a week-long stoppage, while the open pit at Codelco’s El Teniente remains shut after a deadly landslide .

Click on chart for live prices.

Copper’s 2026 advance has forecasters raising their numbers for the second time in three months, and with the metal averaging $13,471 a tonne for the year to date, the 2026 revisions mostly bring the sheet into line with the tape.

Macquarie now has copper averaging $13,573 this year, BMO Capital Markets $13,619 and BMI, a unit of Fitch Solutions, $13,500, up from the $12,700 it moved to in July . The differences open up from next year, and they come down to how much of the 1.5 to 2 million tonnes of copper now sitting in the United States is counted as surplus.

“The great copper gamble”

Macquarie, which in July called the rally “running ahead of reality” , has lifted its 2027 average by 14% to $12,750 and pushed the cycle low to $12,000 in the fourth quarter of next year from $11,000 a quarter earlier, while its long-term price rises to $10,500 a tonne in 2025 dollars.

Prices “have disconnected from the fundamentals and could arguably move higher or lower depending on the outcome of the Section 232,” the bank’s strategists write in a quarterly compendium whose copper chapter is headed “The great copper gamble”, listing the metal among its preferred commodities for the next six to nine months “but very binary”.

The fundamentals as Macquarie counts them are a 223,000-tonne surplus this year after a 531,000-tonne disruption allowance, and surpluses averaging more than 700,000 tonnes a year from 2027 as mine supply grows 4.9% next year and 4.3% in 2028, with Collahuasi, Grasberg, Kamoa-Kakula and Centinela ramping up, Tia Maria starting and Cobre Panama back in full from mid-2027.

Global demand growth slows to 1.5% in 2027 on its numbers, with none at all in China, where construction-related copper use is shrinking 9% a year and air conditioner makers are “again looking at aluminium substitution.”

Visible stocks worldwide are up 300,000 tonnes this year, but that is the US build; everywhere else they are down 168,000 tonnes, and Macquarie says sentiment will not turn until LME and Shanghai inventories start rising again, either quickly on a tariff decision or gradually as its forecast surpluses feed through.

Macquarie’s four tariff scenarios run from a January 1 that passes with no announcement at all, which it rates most likely, to a definitive decision against a duty, which it rates least likely: “the CME price will most likely collapse, taking the LME price with it, and the arb will invert,” with surplus US stocks reappearing in LME warehouses in the US and Asia.

A tariff announced six to eight weeks ahead of implementation would pull a last wave of metal into the US and leave the rest of the world “very tight”, while a formal six-month delay would see the spread fade as it did for platinum and palladium after the critical minerals decision.

Expectations are also growing that a scrap export ban will be folded into any decision; an immediate ban would take about 600,000 tonnes a year of contained copper off the world market.

“Has the market misread US inventory?”

BMO Capital Markets arrives at a very different place from a similar starting point. Its quarterly price deck, published two days before Macquarie’s, raises its long-term copper price by 47% to $16,000 a tonne in real terms, or $18,000 nominal by 2030, with $14,675 for 2027 and $16,000 for 2028, and the bank puts itself 46% above consensus on the long-term number. Its market balance is close to balanced throughout: an 83,000-tonne surplus this year, then small deficits from 2027.

The argument turns on what the US hoard, now close to 2 million tonnes on BMO’s estimate, or about a year of American consumption, actually represents. China’s refined copper imports have run below trend and its exports above trend since the tariff trade began, a cumulative swing of about 1.6 million tonnes on a net basis, which BMO reads as Beijing allowing its strategic reserve to run down while Washington built one.

“Instead of there being a build in above ground inventory over the last 2 years, there has been a geographical redistribution from ‘not visible’ to ‘visible’, meaning today’s price of ~$14,500-15,000/t is fundamentally supported,” the bank writes. Had China bid for metal alongside the US, “copper prices today would in fact be much, much higher,” and at some point China will want to restock.

BMO expects no tariff decision before the US midterms in November, which may see copper “pause for breath” and keep the Comex-LME spread narrow, but says investors it talks to are coming around to the view that the US stockpile “could simply stay in situ for many more years.”

Rising dependence on scrap, with China’s secondary refined output heading for 3.3 million tonnes this year from 2.8 million, is the other leg of its case: scrap is the marginal unit, and it only comes out at higher prices.

BMI sits between the two. It still views the rally “as having extended beyond what fundamentals alone would suggest” and has the market in a 43,000-tonne surplus this year, but has cut its 2026 mine supply growth forecast to 1.1% from 2.4% with Chilean output down 4%, and expects a deficit from 2027 that widens to 1.7 million tonnes by 2035 as demand grows 3% to 4% a year on grids, EVs and data centres.

Its 2027 forecast is $12,900, rising to $15,000 in 2029 and an unchanged $17,000 in 2035. The International Copper Study Group, meeting this week, lifted its 2026 surplus to 104,000 tonnes and kept 2027 at 368,000 tonnes.

The arb has gone, the metal has not

The spread that built the US stockpile has all but disappeared on a spot basis. Comex October copper at $6.62 a pound trades below LME cash, which at Tuesday’s $14,741 works out to $6.69, and John Gross of The Copper Journal calculates the month-to-date average has flipped to an 85-point LME premium from a 17-cent Comex premium in June.

Most of that is London’s doing: the backwardation that put cash $164.50 over three months at Monday’s settlement, since narrowed to $115.50, reflects how little spot metal is left outside the US.

Aurubis, Europe’s largest copper producer, has offered customers a record premium of $347 a tonne for 2027 supply, 10% above this year’s level, Benchmark Minerals reported, and a company spokesperson told Bloomberg that “a lot of material has relocated to the US, leaving warehouses quite empty.”

Further down the curve the premium survives. December Comex at $14,704 a tonne sits about $170 over LME three-month, which Macquarie read at the end of September as the market pricing a 10% chance of a 15% duty (on Wednesday’s prices the same arithmetic gives about 8%).

That is too little to pull fresh shipments across the Atlantic, but enough to keep what is already there in place as long as the Comex curve pays traders to hold it. The tonnes still arriving are cargo booked months ago: Comex stocks rose another 6,500 tonnes last week to 713,000 tonnes, with 100,000 tonnes of African and South American copper due through October.

Deutsche Bank takes the stockpiling argument furthest. Daniel Ghali, the bank’s new head of metals research, told the Wall Street Journal that with China adding to its strategic reserve for decades and the tariff threat pulling metal into American sheds, the two countries could be sitting on 71% of the world’s supply by the end of the year. On that trajectory copper “simply won’t be available” to users elsewhere by the end of 2028, an outcome averted only by prices high enough to force substitution into aluminium.

He sees $10 a pound, or $22,050 a tonne, in the second quarter of 2027, almost 50% above current levels. Even a decision against tariffs may not free the metal, he told the paper, since the LME has warehouses in the US and copper may simply be shuffled between American sites rather than leave the country.

Gross points to copper’s premium over aluminium, which hit a record $5.08 a pound in September, more than double its July 2022 low. “Clearly, this rising premium cannot continue indefinitely, but who among us will step forward to say it’s at the top?” he writes. His September monthly report makes the longer point: China consumed 58.9% of the world’s refined copper last year, up from 12.4% in 2000. “There are too many copper eggs in China’s basket.”

Miners still pricing $5 copper

Copper producers fell with the metal on Wednesday, Lundin Mining down 3.9%, Freeport-McMoRan 3.7%, Southern Copper 3.3% and Teck Resources 2.9%, but the year has been kind. Southern Copper is up 44.1% in 2026, taking its market value to $169 billion, with Glencore ahead 38.6%, BHP 38.0% and Freeport 37.4% at a $100 billion valuation. Teck has gained 36.1% and Anglo American 29.2%. Lundin has managed 13.0%, Antofagasta 7.5% with Centinela on strike, and First Quantum 3.0%.

RBC Capital Markets calculates that North American copper producers at 1.0 times net asset value imply a copper price of $5.03 a pound, from $5.98 for Freeport down to $3.96 for Ivanhoe Mines, against a futures price near $6.70. The group trades at 0.9 times net asset value, in line with its 10-year average.

Comex copper is up more than 18% in 2026.

Top 50 mining companies take $264 billion hit as gold trade unwinds, lithium stocks exit

item.title: テンセントがオラクルからAI半導体10万個をリース、70億ドル規模－FT
item.description:
（ブルームバーグ）： 中国のテンセント・ホールディングス（騰訊）は、東南アジアでオラクルから先端のAI半導体を借り受けることで合意した。テンセントにとってAI半導体のリース契約としては過去最大規模となる。英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（FT）が事情に詳しい関係者の話として報じた。
報道によると、テンセントは、5年間の契約の一環として10万個の半導体を利用できるようになる。契約額は70億ドル（約1兆1000億円）に上るという。
中国のAI開発企業は米国の輸出規制を回避するため、米エヌビディア製など中国国内では入手できないAIアクセラレーターを海外で借りて利用している。中国のテクノロジー企業は、東南アジアのデータセンターの最大顧客層の一つとなっている。
テンセントとオラクルの担当者は、ブルームバーグ・ニュースのコメント要請に直ちに応じなかった。
原題：Tencent Leases AI Chips From Oracle
